title.zh: 卷三十六 列傳第二十四: 薛辯 薛寘 薛憕
title.en: Volume 36 Biographies 24: Xue Bian, Xue Zhi, Xue Cheng
title.raw: 卷三十六 列傳第二十四: 薛辯 薛寘 薛憕 Volume 36 Biographies 24: Xue Bian, Xue Zhi, Xue Cheng

sentences.zh: 薛辯 薛寘 薛憕

translations.literal: Xue Bian; Xue Zhi; Xue Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bian, Xue Zhi, and Xue Cheng

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十四

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty-Four
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 24

sentences.zh: 薛辯五世孫端端子胄端從子浚端從祖弟湖湖子聰聰子孝通孝通子道衡聰弟子善善弟慎薛寘薛憕

translations.literal: Xue Bian's fifth-generation descendant Duan; Duan's son Zhou; Duan's collateral descendant Jun; Duan's first cousin once removed Hu; Hu's son Cong; Cong's son Xiaotong; Xiaotong's son Daoheng; Cong's collateral nephew Shan; Shan's younger brother Shen; Xue Zhi; Xue Cheng
translations.idiomatic: The line continues through Xue Bian's fifth-generation descendant Duan and his son Zhou, Duan's collateral descendant Jun, and Duan's first cousin once removed Hu; through Hu's son Cong and Cong's son Xiaotong to Xiaotong's son Daoheng; through Cong's collateral nephew Shan and Shan's younger brother Shen; and separately Xue Zhi and Xue Cheng

sentences.zh: 薛辯，字允白，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Bian, styled Yunbai, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bian, styled Yunbai, was from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖興，晉尚書右僕射、冀州刺史、安邑公，諡曰：莊。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xing was Jin Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Inspector of Jizhou, and Duke of Anyi; his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xing had served as Jin Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Jizhou and held the title Duke of Anyi; he was posthumously known as Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 祖濤襲爵，位梁州刺史，諡曰忠惠。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tao inherited the title, held the post of Inspector of Liangzhou, and was posthumously titled Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tao inherited the family title, served as Inspector of Liangzhou, and was posthumously known as Zhonghui.

sentences.zh: 京都傾覆，皆以義烈著聞。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, both were renowned for righteous valor.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was overrun, both men became famous for their righteous courage.

sentences.zh: 父強，字威明，幼有大志，懷軍國籌略。

translations.literal: His father Qiang, styled Weiming, had great ambitions in youth and harbored strategies for army and state.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiang, styled Weiming, had shown great ambition from youth and kept in mind plans for army and state.

sentences.zh: 與北海王猛，同志友善。

translations.literal: With Wang Meng of Beihai he shared the same aims and were close friends.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wang Meng of Beihai were kindred spirits and close friends.

sentences.zh: 及桓溫入關中，猛以巾褐謁之。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen entered Guanzhong, Meng went to see him in plain cloth and headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen marched into Guanzhong, Meng went to see him dressed as a common scholar in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「江東無卿比也，秦國定多奇士，如生輩尚有幾人？

translations.literal: Wen said: "East of the Yangtze has no one to compare with you; Qin must have many extraordinary men—how many like you are there still?
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "There is no one like you east of the Yangtze. Qin must have many remarkable men—how many more are there like you?

sentences.zh: 吾欲與之俱南。

translations.literal: I wish to go south with them together.
translations.idiomatic: I would like to take them south with me.

sentences.zh: 」猛曰：「公求可與撥亂濟時者，友人薛威明其人也。

translations.literal: " Meng said: "Your lordship seeks one who can set chaos aright and rescue the age—my friend Xue Weiming is such a man.
translations.idiomatic: " Meng replied, "If you are looking for someone who can set chaos aright and rescue the age, my friend Xue Weiming is the man.

sentences.zh: 」溫曰：「聞之久矣。

translations.literal: " Wen said: "I have heard of him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen said, "I have heard of him for a long time.

sentences.zh: 」方致朝命。

translations.literal: " He was just about to send court orders.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen was on the point of issuing a court summons.

sentences.zh: 強聞之，自商山來謁，與猛皆署軍謀祭酒。

translations.literal: Qiang heard of it and came from Shangshan to pay his respects; he and Meng were both appointed Army Strategy Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang heard of this, he came down from Mount Shang to present himself, and both he and Meng were appointed Army Strategy Libationers.

sentences.zh: 強察溫有大志而無成功，乃勸猛止。

translations.literal: Qiang perceived that Wen had great ambition but would not succeed, and so urged Meng to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang saw that Wen had great ambition but would never succeed, and urged Meng to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 俄而溫敗。

translations.literal: Before long Wen was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Wen was defeated.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅立，猛見委任。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian came to the throne, Meng was entrusted with office.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian came to the throne, Meng was given important responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 其平陽公融為書，將以車馬聘強。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pingyang, Rong, wrote a letter intending to invite Qiang with carriage and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pingyang, Rong, wrote offering to fetch Qiang with carriage and horses.

sentences.zh: 猛以為不可屈，乃止。

translations.literal: Meng thought he could not be bent and so stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Meng judged that Qiang could not be coerced, and the invitation was dropped.

sentences.zh: 及堅如河東伐張平，自與數百騎馳至強壘下，求與相見。

translations.literal: When Jian went to Hedong to attack Zhang Ping, he himself galloped with several hundred horsemen to below Qiang's fortress and asked to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian marched into Hedong to attack Zhang Ping, he rode ahead with several hundred horsemen to Qiang's fortress and asked for an audience.

sentences.zh: 強使主簿責之。

translations.literal: Qiang sent his registrar to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang sent his registrar to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 因慷慨宣言曰：「此城終無生降之臣，但有死節之將耳。

translations.literal: He then made a spirited declaration, saying: "This city will never have a minister who surrenders alive—only generals who die for principle.
translations.idiomatic: He then declared with passion, "This city will never yield a minister who surrenders alive—only generals who die holding their post.

sentences.zh: 」堅諸將請攻之，堅曰：「須吾平晉，自當面縛。

translations.literal: " Jian's generals asked to attack him; Jian said: "Wait until I pacify Jin—he will bind himself and come before me.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian's generals urged an attack, but Jian said, "When I have pacified Jin, he will come and bind himself before me.

sentences.zh: 舍之以勸事君者。

translations.literal: Spare him to encourage those who serve their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be, as an example to encourage loyal service.

sentences.zh: 」後堅伐晉，軍敗，強遂總宗室強兵，威振河輔，破慕容永于陳川。

translations.literal: " Later, when Jian attacked Jin and his army was defeated, Qiang then gathered the clan's strong troops, his prestige shaking the He region and its approaches, and defeated Murong Yong at Chenchuan.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, when Jian's campaign against Jin ended in defeat, Qiang rallied the clan's fighting men, his authority shaking the Yellow River region, and defeated Murong Yong at Chenchuan.

sentences.zh: 姚興聞而憚之，遣使重加禮命，徵拜右光祿大夫、七兵尚書，封馮翊郡公，轉左戶尚書。

translations.literal: Yao Xing heard and feared him, sent envoys with repeated honors and appointments, summoned and appointed him Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Director of the Seven Armies, enfeoffed as Duke of Fengyi Commandery, then transferred to Director of the Left Households.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing heard of him and was wary; he sent envoys with repeated honors and summoned Qiang to serve as Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Director of the Seven Armies, enfeoffing him as Duke of Fengyi and later transferring him to Director of the Left Households.

sentences.zh: 年九十八，卒。

translations.literal: At age ninety-eight he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of ninety-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國大將軍、司徙公，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given General Who Assists the State and Duke of Situ; his posthumous title was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Assists the State and Duke of Situ, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 辯幼而俊爽，俶儻多大略，由是豪傑多歸慕之。

translations.literal: Bian in youth was handsome and alert, unconventional and possessed of great strategy; because of this many heroes came to admire and follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was handsome and quick-witted from youth, bold and far-seeing, and many men of consequence came to admire him.

sentences.zh: 強卒，復襲統其營。

translations.literal: When Qiang died, he again inherited command of his camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang died, he again took command of his father's forces.

sentences.zh: 仕姚興，曆太子中庶子、河北太守。

translations.literal: He served Yao Xing, successively as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Yao Xing as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and later as Administrator of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 辯知姚氏運衰，遂棄歸家保鄉邑。

translations.literal: Bian knew the Yao clan's fortune was declining and so abandoned office, returned home, and guarded his native district.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Yao house was in decline, Bian resigned and went home to defend his native district.

sentences.zh: 及晉將劉裕平姚泓，即署相國掾。

translations.literal: When the Jin general Liu Yu pacified Yao Hong, he was at once appointed Aide to the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin general Liu Yu overthrew Yao Hong, Bian was appointed Aide to the Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 尋除平陽太守，委以北道鎮捍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Administrator of Pingyang, entrusted with guarding the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Administrator of Pingyang and charged with holding the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 及長安失守。

translations.literal: When Chang'an fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an fell,

sentences.zh: 辯遂歸魏。

translations.literal: Bian then went over to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Bian went over to Wei.

sentences.zh: 仍立功於河際，位平西將軍、東雍州刺史，賜爵汾陰侯。

translations.literal: He again achieved merit on the river frontier, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: He won further distinction on the Yellow River frontier, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 其年詣闕，明元深加器重，明年方得旋鎮。

translations.literal: That year he came to court; Mingyuan greatly valued him, and only the next year was he able to return to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That year he presented himself at court; Emperor Mingyuan held him in high regard, and he was not able to return to his post until the following year.

sentences.zh: 帝謂之曰：「朕委卿西蕃，志在關右，卿宜克終良算，與朕為長安主人。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "I entrust you with the western territories; my aim is Guanzhong—you should carry your good plans through to the end and be lord of Chang'an for me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "I am entrusting you with the western frontier; my aim is Guanzhong. Carry your plans through to the end and be master of Chang'an on my behalf.

sentences.zh: 」辯既還任，務農教戰。

translations.literal: " When Bian had returned to his post, he devoted himself to farming and training for war.
translations.idiomatic: " On returning to his post, Bian devoted himself to agriculture and military training.

sentences.zh: 恆以數千之眾，摧抗赫連氏。

translations.literal: Constantly with a force of several thousand he broke and resisted the Helian clan.
translations.idiomatic: With only a few thousand men he repeatedly held off the Helian.

sentences.zh: 帝甚褒獎之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 又除并州刺史，征授大羽真。

translations.literal: He was further made Inspector of Bingzhou and summoned to receive the title of Grand Yuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Inspector of Bingzhou and summoned to receive the title Grand Yuzhen.

sentences.zh: 泰常七年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taichang he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taichang he died in office.

sentences.zh: 帝以所圖未遂，深悼惜之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because his plans had not been realized, deeply mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned him, for his own designs in the west had not yet been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 贈並、雍二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the posts of Inspector of Bing and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Inspector of Bing and Yong.

sentences.zh: 子謹，字法順。

translations.literal: His son Jin, styled Fashun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin, styled Fashun,

sentences.zh: 容貌魁偉，高才博學。

translations.literal: was imposing in appearance, of lofty talent and broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: was imposing in bearing, gifted, and widely learned.

sentences.zh: 隨劉裕度江，位府記室參軍。

translations.literal: He followed Liu Yu across the Yangtze and held the post of Registrar in the Princely Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangtze with Liu Yu and served as Registrar in the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 辯將歸魏，密報謹，謹遂亦來奔。

translations.literal: When Bian was about to go over to Wei, he secretly informed Jin, and Jin then also came to defect.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian prepared to go over to Wei, he sent word secretly to Jin, who then defected as well.

sentences.zh: 授河東太守，後襲爵汾陰侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Hedong and later inherited the title Marquis of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of Hedong and later inherited the marquisate of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 始光三年，與宜都王奚斤共討赫連昌，禽其東平公乙兜，克蒲阪。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shiguang, together with the Prince of Yidu, Xi Jin, he attacked Helian Chang, captured his Prince of Dongping, Yidou, and took Puban.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shiguang he joined the Prince of Yidu, Xi Jin, in attacking Helian Chang, captured Helian's Prince of Dongping, Yidou, and took Puban.

sentences.zh: 遂以新舊百姓並為一郡，除平西將軍，復為太守。

translations.literal: He then combined old and new populations into one commandery, was made General Who Pacifies the West, and again served as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He merged the old and new populations into a single commandery, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, and again served as administrator.

sentences.zh: 神蒨三年，除使持節、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenqi he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenqi he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 山胡白龍憑險作逆，太武詔南陽公奚眷與謹並為都將，討平之，封涪陵郡公。

translations.literal: The Mountain Hu leader Bailong relied on terrain to rebel; Emperor Taiwu ordered the Prince of Nanyang, Xi Juan, and Jin jointly as chief generals to suppress and pacify him; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Fuling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mountain Hu leader Bailong rebelled from mountain strongholds, Emperor Taiwu ordered the Prince of Nanyang, Xi Juan, and Jin to serve jointly as chief generals and put down the revolt; Jin was enfeoffed as Duke of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 太延初，征吐沒骨，平之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiyan he campaigned against Tuguhun and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taiyan he campaigned against Tuguhun and subdued them.

sentences.zh: 謹自郡遷州，威恩兼被，風化大行。

translations.literal: When Jin moved from commandery to province, both authority and kindness extended over all, and civilizing influence flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin moved from commandery to provincial office, his authority and kindness reached everyone, and civilizing influence spread widely.

sentences.zh: 時兵荒之後，儒雅道息，謹命立庠序，教以詩書。

translations.literal: At that time, after the ravages of war, Confucian learning had faded; Jin ordered schools established and taught the Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of war, classical learning had fallen silent; Jin ordered schools built and had the people taught the Odes and Documents.

sentences.zh: 三農之暇，悉令受業，躬巡邑裏，親加考試，河汾之地，儒道更興。

translations.literal: In the intervals of the three agricultural seasons he had all receive instruction; he personally toured the districts and examined them himself; in the He and Fen region, Confucian learning revived.
translations.idiomatic: In the slack seasons of the farming year he had everyone attend school; he toured the districts in person to examine the students, and learning flourished again along the Fen and Yellow Rivers.

sentences.zh: 真君元年，征授內都坐大官，輔政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenjun he was summoned and appointed Grand Master of the Inner Court and assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenjun he was summoned to court as Grand Master of the Inner Court and took part in governing.

sentences.zh: 深見賞重，每訪以政道，車駕臨幸者前後數四。

translations.literal: He was deeply valued and rewarded; the emperor repeatedly consulted him on the way of government; the imperial carriage visited him on four separate occasions.
translations.idiomatic: He was held in deep esteem; the emperor often sought his counsel on governance, and the imperial carriage visited him on four occasions.

sentences.zh: 後從駕北討，與中山王辰等後期，見殺。

translations.literal: Later he followed the emperor on the northern campaign; he and the Prince of Zhongshan, Chen, and others were late and were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a northern campaign, he and the Prince of Zhongshan, Chen, and others fell behind schedule and were executed.

sentences.zh: 尋贈鎮西將軍、秦雍二州刺史，諡曰元公。

translations.literal: Soon he was posthumously given General Who Guards the West and the posts of Inspector of Qin and Yong; his posthumous title was Duke Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posthumously honored as General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Qin and Yong, with the posthumous name Duke Yuan.

sentences.zh: 長子初古拔，一曰車轂拔，本名洪祚，太武賜名焉。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chuguba, also called Cheguba, original name Hongzuo; Taiwu bestowed his name.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chuguba—also called Cheguba, originally named Hongzuo—received his name from Emperor Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 沈毅有器識。

translations.literal: He was deep, resolute, and possessed judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He was steady, resolute, and discerning.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，司徙崔浩見而奇之。

translations.literal: At his capping, Situ Cui Hao saw him and considered him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, Cui Hao, Duke of Situ, met him and was struck by his ability.

sentences.zh: 真君中，蓋吳擾動關右，薛永宗屯據河側，太武親討之。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era, Gai Wu stirred up trouble in Guanxi; Xue Yongzong held the river bank; Taiwu personally campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun era, Gai Wu raised disturbances in Guanxi and Xue Yongzong held the riverbank; Emperor Taiwu campaigned against them in person.

sentences.zh: 詔拔糾合宗鄉，壁於河際，斷二寇往來之路。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ba to gather the clan and native district, fortify on the river bank, and cut the two rebels' route of communication.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Ba to rally the clan and local communities, fortify the riverbank, and sever the rebels' lines of communication.

sentences.zh: 事平，除中散，賜爵永康侯。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 太武南討，以拔為都將，從駕臨江而還。

translations.literal: When Taiwu campaigned south, Ba was made chief general, followed the emperor to the Yangtze, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On Taiwu's southern campaign, Ba served as chief general, accompanied the emperor to the Yangtze, and returned with the army.

sentences.zh: 又共陸真討反氐仇傉檀、強免生，平之。

translations.literal: He again with Lu Zhen attacked the rebellious Di, Chou Lután and Qiang Miansheng, and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Lu Zhen in suppressing the Di rebels Chou Lután and Qiang Miansheng.

sentences.zh: 皇興三年，除散騎常侍，尚文成女西河長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangxing he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, married Emperor Wen's daughter the Princess Chang of Xihe, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangxing he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, married Emperor Wen's daughter the Princess Chang of Xihe, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 其年，拔族叔徐州刺史安都據城歸順，敕拔詣彭城勞迎，除南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: That year Ba's clansman-uncle Andu, Inspector of Xuzhou, held the city and came over in submission; an edict ordered Ba to go to Pengcheng to welcome him with honors, and he was made Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year his clansman-uncle Andu, Inspector of Xuzhou, surrendered his city; Ba was ordered to Pengcheng to welcome him and was appointed Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 延興二年，除鎮西大將軍、開府儀同，進爵平陽公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxing he was made General Who Guards the West with privilege to maintain an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and advanced to Duke of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanxing he was appointed General Who Guards the West with privilege to maintain an office equal to the Three Excellencies and advanced to Duke of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 三年，拔與南兗州刺史游明根、南平太守許含等，以善政征詣京師。

translations.literal: In the third year Ba, together with You Minggen, Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, Xu Han, Administrator of Nanping, and others, were summoned to the capital for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Ba, together with You Minggen, Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, Xu Han, Administrator of Nanping, and others, were summoned to the capital for their excellent administration.

sentences.zh: 獻文親自勞勉，復令還州。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen personally comforted and encouraged them, then ordered them back to their provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen received them in person with praise and sent them back to their posts.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，改爵河東公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe his title was changed to Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe his title was changed to Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左光祿大夫，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 長子胤，字甯宗。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yin, styled Ningzong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yin, styled Ningzong,

sentences.zh: 少有父風。

translations.literal: in youth showed his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: showed his father's character from youth.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，拜中散。

translations.literal: At his capping he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 襲爵鎮西大將軍、河東公，除懸瓠鎮將。

translations.literal: He inherited the title General Who Guards the West and Duke of Hedong, and was made Garrison Commander of Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's rank as General Who Guards the West and Duke of Hedong and was appointed Garrison Commander of Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 尋授持節、義陽道都將。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the Staff of Authority and made Chief General of the Yiyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the Staff of Authority and made Chief General of the Yiyang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 後除立忠將軍、河北太守。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Establishes Loyalty and Administrator of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General Who Establishes Loyalty and Administrator of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 郡帶山河，俗多盜賊。

translations.literal: The commandery lay among mountains and rivers; the customs were full of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery lay among mountains and rivers, and banditry was widespread.

sentences.zh: 有韓、馬兩姓各二千餘家，恃強憑險，最為狡害，劫掠道路，侵暴鄉閭。

translations.literal: The Han and Ma surnames each had more than two thousand households; relying on strength and terrain they were the most cunning and harmful, plundering the roads and oppressing the villages.
translations.idiomatic: The Han and Ma clans each numbered more than two thousand households; trusting in their strength and the difficult terrain, they were the worst offenders, robbing travelers and terrorizing the countryside.

sentences.zh: 胤至郡，即收其奸魁二十餘人，一時戮之。

translations.literal: When Yin reached the commandery, he at once seized more than twenty of their ringleaders and executed them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Yin took office, he arrested more than twenty of their ringleaders and executed them in one sweep.

sentences.zh: 於是群盜懾氣，郡中清肅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandits were cowed and the commandery became clear and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were cowed, and the commandery became peaceful.

sentences.zh: 卒於郡，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died in the commandery; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; his posthumous name was Jing.

sentences.zh: 子裔，字豫孫，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yi, styled Yusun, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, styled Yusun, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 性豪爽，盛營園宅，賓客聲伎，以恣嬉遊。

translations.literal: By nature bold and generous, he lavishly built gardens and mansions, with guests, music, and performers for unrestrained pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed by nature, built lavish estates, and surrounded himself with guests, musicians, and entertainers for endless revelry.

sentences.zh: 卒于洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He died as Inspector of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Inspector of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 子孝紳襲爵，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoshen inherited the title and held the post of Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoshen inherited the title and served as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 孝紳立行險薄，坐事為河南尹元世俊所劾，死。

translations.literal: Xiaoshen's conduct was treacherous and shallow; for an offense he was impeached by Yuan Shijun, Intendant of Henan, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoshen's conduct was treacherous and mean; he was impeached by Yuan Shijun, Intendant of Henan, and put to death.

sentences.zh: 後贈華州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously given Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously honored as Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 拔弟洪隆，字菩提，驎位河東太守。

translations.literal: Ba's younger brother Honglong, styled Puti; Lin held the post of Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Ba's younger brother Honglong, styled Puti; Honglong's son Lin served as Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 長子驎駒，好讀書，舉秀才，除中書博士。

translations.literal: His eldest son Linju loved reading; he was recommended as xiucai and made Doctor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's eldest son Linju was fond of learning; recommended as xiucai, he was appointed Doctor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 齊使至，詔驎駒兼主客郎以接之。

translations.literal: When envoys from Qi arrived, an edict appointed Linju concurrently as Master of Guests to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys from Qi arrived, an edict appointed Linju concurrently Master of Guests to receive them.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈河東太守，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Administrator of Hedong; his posthumous title was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Administrator of Hedong, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 始拔尚西河主，有賜田在馮翊，驎駒徙居之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ba married the Princess of Xihe, there was granted land in Fufeng; Linju moved to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: When Ba had married the Princess of Xihe, the court granted land in Fufeng, and Linju moved his household there.

sentences.zh: 遂家于馮翊之夏陽。

translations.literal: The family then settled at Xiayang in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: The clan thereafter made its home at Xiayang in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 長子慶之，字慶集。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qingzhi, styled Qingji.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Qingzhi, styled Qingji,

sentences.zh: 頗有學業，閑解几案，位廷尉丞。

translations.literal: had considerable learning and was skilled at desk affairs; he held the post of Assistant in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: was well educated and adept at legal paperwork, and served as Assistant in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 廷尉寺鄰北城，曾夏日寺傍得一狐，慶之與廷尉正博陵崔纂，或以城狐狡害，宜速殺之；

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review adjoined the northern wall; once in summer a fox was found beside the court; Qingzhi and the Reviewer Cui Zuan of Boling—some said a city fox was cunning and harmful and should be killed at once;
translations.idiomatic: The court building stood beside the northern city wall. One summer a fox was found near the offices. Qingzhi and the Reviewer Cui Zuan of Boling debated whether, as a city fox and an ill omen, it should be killed immediately;

sentences.zh: 或以長育之月，宜待秋分。

translations.literal: others said that in the month of growing and nurturing one should wait until the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: or whether, in the season of growth and nurture, they should wait until the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 二卿裴延俊、袁翻，互有同異。

translations.literal: The two ministers Pei Yanjun and Yuan Fan each had agreement and disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers Pei Yanjun and Yuan Fan took opposing sides.

sentences.zh: 雖曰戲謔，詞義可觀，事傳於世。

translations.literal: Though called banter, the words and meaning were worth viewing; the affair was transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Though offered in jest, their arguments were eloquent, and the story became widely known.

sentences.zh: 後兼左丞，為並、肆行台，賜爵龍丘子，行滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as Left Vice Director, was made Mobile Office for Bing and Xi, enfeoffed as Viscount of Longqiu, and acted as Inspector of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as Left Vice Director, headed the mobile office for Bing and Xi, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Longqiu, and acted as Inspector of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 為葛榮攻圍，城陷。

translations.literal: He was besieged by Ge Rong and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong besieged the city, it fell.

sentences.zh: 尋患，卒，贈華州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill and died; he was posthumously given Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and died, and was posthumously honored as Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 慶之弟英集，性通率。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's younger brother Yingji was by nature open and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi's younger brother Yingji was frank and unpretentious by nature.

sentences.zh: 隨舅李崇在揚州，以軍功累至書侍御史、通直散騎常侍，卒。

translations.literal: He followed his maternal uncle Li Chong in Yangzhou; through military merit he rose to Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry with Unimpeded Access, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his uncle Li Chong to Yangzhou and, through military service, rose to Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry with Unimpeded Access before his death.

sentences.zh: 英集子端。

translations.literal: Yingji's son was Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Yingji's son was Duan.

sentences.zh: 端字仁直，本名沙陀。

translations.literal: Duan, styled Renzhi, original name Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: Duan, styled Renzhi, was originally named Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 有志操，遭父憂，居喪合禮。

translations.literal: He had aspiration and integrity; when his father died he observed mourning in accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of principle; when his father died he observed mourning with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 與弟裕勵精篤學，不交人事。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Yu he urged themselves on in devoted study and did not mingle in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Yu devoted themselves to study and kept aloof from worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 年十七，司空高乾邕辟為參軍。

translations.literal: At age seventeen the Minister of Works Gao Qianyou recruited him as Aide.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he was recruited as an aide by Gao Qianyou, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 賜爵平陰男。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyin.

sentences.zh: 端以天下擾亂，遂棄官歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Duan, because the realm was in turmoil, then abandoned office and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire fell into chaos, Duan resigned his post and returned home.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，周文令大都督薛崇禮據龍門，引端同行。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Zhou Wen ordered the Grand Commander Xue Chongli to hold Longmen and took Duan along with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Zhou Wen ordered Grand Commander Xue Chongli to hold Longmen and took Duan with him.

sentences.zh: 崇禮尋失守，降東魏。

translations.literal: Chongli soon lost his hold and surrendered to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chongli soon lost the position and surrendered to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣行台薛修義督乙幹貴西度，據楊氏壁。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent the Mobile Office Xue Xiuyi supervising Yigan Gui to cross west and hold the Yang clan rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Mobile Office Xue Xiuyi, directing Yigan Gui, to cross west and seize the Yang clan fort.

sentences.zh: 與宗親及家僮等先在壁中，修義乃令其兵逼端等東度。

translations.literal: He was with kinsmen and household servants already inside the rampart; Xiuyi then ordered his troops to force Duan and the others to cross east.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was inside the fort with his kinsmen and household retainers when Xiuyi ordered his troops to force them to cross east.

sentences.zh: 方欲濟河，會日暮，端密與宗室及家僮等叛之。

translations.literal: Just as they were about to cross the river, night fell; Duan secretly rebelled with the clan and household servants.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to cross the river, night fell, and Duan secretly turned on them with his kinsmen and retainers.

sentences.zh: 修義亦遣騎追，端且戰且馳，遂入石城柵，得免。

translations.literal: Xiuyi also sent cavalry in pursuit; Duan fought as he fled and entered the Shicheng stockade, escaping harm.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi sent cavalry in pursuit; Duan fought his way free and reached the Shicheng stockade.

sentences.zh: 柵中先有百家，端與並力固守。

translations.literal: In the stockade were already a hundred households; Duan joined them in stout defense.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred households were already in the stockade, and Duan joined them in a determined defense.

sentences.zh: 貴等數來慰喻，知端無降意，遂拔還河東。

translations.literal: Gui and others came several times to comfort and persuade; knowing Duan had no intent to surrender, they withdrew to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Gui came repeatedly to win him over, but seeing Duan would not submit, withdrew to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 東魏又遣其將賀蘭懿、南汾州刺史薛琰達守楊氏壁。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei again sent its generals Helan Yi and the Inspector of Southern Fenzhou Xue Yanda to hold the Yang clan rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Generals Helan Yi and Xue Yanda, Inspector of Southern Fenzhou, to hold the Yang fort.

sentences.zh: 端率其屬，並招喻村人，多設奇兵以臨之。

translations.literal: Duan led his followers, also summoning and persuading villagers, and set many ambush troops to press them.
translations.idiomatic: Duan rallied his followers, won over the local villagers, and deployed ambushes against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 懿等疑有大軍，便東遁，赴船溺死者數千人。

translations.literal: Yi and the others suspected a great army and fled east; several thousand drowned rushing for boats.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his men, fearing a large force, fled east; thousands drowned trying to reach their boats.

sentences.zh: 端收其器械，復還楊氏壁。

translations.literal: Duan gathered their weapons and returned again to the Yang clan rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Duan seized their arms and returned to the Yang fort.

sentences.zh: 周文遣南汾州刺史蘇景恕鎮之。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen sent the Inspector of Southern Fenzhou Su Jingshu to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen sent Su Jingshu, Inspector of Southern Fenzhou, to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 降書勞問，征端赴闕，以為大丞相府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: A letter of surrender comforted and inquired; Duan was summoned to court and made Aide in the Households Section of the Grand Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen sent a letter of commendation and summoned Duan to court as Aide in the Households Section of the Grand Chancellor's Office.

sentences.zh: 從禽竇泰，復弘農，戰沙苑，並有功，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shayuan—all with merit—and was advanced to Baron.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shayuan, winning distinction in each, and was advanced to Baron.

sentences.zh: 後改封交城縣伯，累遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Later his enfeoffment was changed to Baron of Jiaocheng County; he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was later re-enfeoffed as Baron of Jiaocheng and rose to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 端性強直，每有奏請，不避權貴。

translations.literal: Duan's nature was forceful and upright; whenever he submitted memorials he did not avoid the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was forceful and upright; in his memorials he never shrank from the powerful.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉之，故賜名端，欲令名質相副。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen praised this and therefore bestowed the name Duan, wishing name and substance to match.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen approved and bestowed the name Duan so that his name would match his character.

sentences.zh: 自居選曹，先盡賢能，雖貴遊子弟，才劣行薄者，未嘗升擢之。

translations.literal: Once he held the selection office, he put the worthy and able first; even sons of noble houses, if talent was poor and conduct shallow, were never promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the selection office he put merit first; even sons of great families were never promoted if their talent or conduct fell short.

sentences.zh: 每啟周文云：「設官分職，本康時務，苟非其人，不如曠職。

translations.literal: He often reported to Zhou Wen: "Establishing offices and dividing duties is fundamentally to bring peace to the age's tasks; if it is not the right person, better to leave the post vacant.
translations.idiomatic: He often told Zhou Wen, "Offices exist to secure the peace of the age; if the wrong man holds a post, it is better left vacant.

sentences.zh: 」周文深然之。

translations.literal: " Zhou Wen deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Wen strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 大統十六年，軍東討，柱國李弼為別道元帥，妙簡英寮，數日不定。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong the army campaigned east; the Pillar of State Li Bi was separate-route commander-in-chief and for several days could not settle on excellent staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Datong, when the army marched east, Pillar of State Li Bi, commanding a separate column, spent days unable to choose his staff.

sentences.zh: 周文謂弼曰：「為公思得一長史，無過薛端。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen said to Bi: "Thinking for you to obtain a chief secretary, none surpasses Xue Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen told Bi, "For your chief secretary, no one surpasses Xue Duan.

sentences.zh: 」弼對曰：「真才也」乃遣之。

translations.literal: " Bi replied: "Truly talented," and sent for him.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi replied, "A true talent," and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書右丞，仍掌選事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and still managed selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing while continuing to oversee appointments.

sentences.zh: 梁主蕭察曾獻馬瑙鐘，周文帝執之顧丞郎曰：「能擲摴蒱頭得盧者，便與鐘。

translations.literal: Liang ruler Xiao Cha once presented an agate bell; Zhou Wendi held it and turned to the directorate aides, saying: "Whoever can throw the dice and get Lu shall have the bell.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler Xiao Cha once presented an agate bell. Zhou Wendi held it up and told the directorate aides, "Whoever throws the dice and rolls Lu may have the bell.

sentences.zh: 」已經數人不得。

translations.literal: " Several men already had not succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: " Several had already tried and failed.

sentences.zh: 頃至端，乃執摴[HT]蒱頭而言曰：「非為此鐘可貴，但思露其誠耳。

translations.literal: Soon it came to Duan; he took the dice and said: "It is not that this bell is precious—I only wish to show my sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan's turn came, he took the dice and said, "It is not the bell I prize, but the chance to show my sincerity.

sentences.zh: 」便擲之，五子皆黑。

translations.literal: " He threw, and all five were black.
translations.idiomatic: " He threw, and all five dice came up black.

sentences.zh: 文帝大悅，即以賜之。

translations.literal: Wendi was greatly pleased and at once gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi was delighted and gave him the bell on the spot.

sentences.zh: 魏帝廢，近臣有勸文帝踐極，文帝召端告之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor was deposed; close ministers urged Wendi to ascend the throne; Wendi summoned Duan and told him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei emperor was deposed, courtiers urged Wendi to take the throne; Wendi summoned Duan and confided his plans.

sentences.zh: 端以為三方未一，遽正名號，示天下以不廣。

translations.literal: Duan thought the three regions were not yet unified; to hastily rectify the title would show the realm a lack of breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Duan argued that the realm was not yet united and that to proclaim himself emperor too soon would show a lack of magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 請待龕翦僭偽，然後俯順樂推。

translations.literal: He asked to wait until the usurpers were cut down, then humbly follow the people's willing elevation.
translations.idiomatic: He urged waiting until the rival regimes were destroyed, then accepting the people's acclaim.

sentences.zh: 文帝撫端背曰：「成我者卿也。

translations.literal: Wendi stroked Duan's back and said: "You have made me what I am.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi clapped Duan on the back and said, "You have made me what I am.

sentences.zh: 卿心既與我同，身豈與我異。

translations.literal: Your heart is already one with mine—how could your person be different from mine?
translations.idiomatic: Your heart is already one with mine—how could your person be apart from mine?

sentences.zh: 」遂脫所著冠帶袍褲並以賜之。

translations.literal: " He then removed the cap, belt, robe, and trousers he was wearing and bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then stripped off his own cap, belt, robe, and trousers and gave them to Duan.

sentences.zh: 進授吏部尚書，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He was advanced and appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 端久處選曹，雅有人倫之鑒，其所擢用，咸得其才。

translations.literal: Duan had long been in the selection office and elegantly possessed judgment of human worth; those he promoted all obtained their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Long service in the selection office had given Duan a keen eye for talent, and those he promoted invariably proved capable.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜軍司馬，加侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established he was appointed Army Major; added Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies; advanced to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established he was made Army Major, then Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies, and advanced to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，再遷戶部中大夫，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended, he was again promoted to Grand Master of the Households Section and advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou came to the throne, Duan was promoted to Grand Master of the Households Section and advanced to Duke.

sentences.zh: 晉公護將廢帝，召群臣議之。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu was about to depose the emperor and summoned the ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Hu planned to depose the emperor, he summoned the ministers for counsel.

sentences.zh: 端頗具同異，護不悅，出為蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: Duan offered considerable agreement and disagreement; Hu was displeased and sent him out as Inspector of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan spoke strongly against the move; Hu was displeased and sent him out as Inspector of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 為政寬惠，人吏愛之。

translations.literal: His governance was lenient and kind; officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and benevolent, and officials and commoners alike loved him.

sentences.zh: 轉基州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 基州地接梁、陳，事藉鎮撫，總管史甯遣司馬梁榮催令赴任。

translations.literal: Jizhou's territory bordered Liang and Chen; affairs relied on pacification; the Commander-in-Chief Shi Ning sent the Major Liang Rong to urge him to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou bordered Liang and Chen and needed firm administration; Commander-in-Chief Shi Ning sent Major Liang Rong to hurry him to his post.

sentences.zh: 蔡州父老訴榮，請留端者千餘人。

translations.literal: The elders of Caizhou appealed to Rong; more than a thousand asked to keep Duan.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand elders of Caizhou petitioned Rong to keep Duan.

sentences.zh: 至基州未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Not long after reaching Jizhou he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had not long been in Jizhou when he died.

sentences.zh: 遺誡薄葬，府州贈遺，勿有所受。

translations.literal: His testament enjoined simple burial; gifts from prefecture and province were not to be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions for a simple burial and forbade his family to accept gifts from the prefecture or province.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加大將軍，進封文城郡公，諡曰質。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given his former office, added Grand General, advanced to Duke of Wencheng Commandery; his posthumous title was Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with his former offices, made Grand General, advanced to Duke of Wencheng, and given the posthumous name Zhi.

sentences.zh: 子胄嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhou inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 胄字紹玄，少聰明，每覽異書，便曉其義。

translations.literal: Zhou, styled Shaoxuan, was clever in youth; whenever he read unusual books he at once understood their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, styled Shaoxuan, was clever from youth; whenever he read an unusual book he grasped its meaning at once.

sentences.zh: 常歎訓注者不會聖人深旨，輒以意辯之，諸儒莫不稱善。

translations.literal: He often sighed that commentators did not grasp the sages' deep intent and would argue according to his own understanding; the Confucians all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He often lamented that commentators missed the sages' deeper meaning and would argue from his own understanding, to the admiration of other scholars.

sentences.zh: 性慷慨，志立功名。

translations.literal: By nature generous, his ambition was to establish merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous by nature and aspired to win merit and renown.

sentences.zh: 周明帝時，襲爵文城郡公。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Wencheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming of Zhou he inherited the dukedom of Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷上儀同，尋拜司金大夫，後加開府。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Senior Pillar of State; soon made Grand Master of the Metals Office; later added privilege to maintain an office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Senior Pillar of State, was made Grand Master of the Metals Office, and later granted privilege to maintain an office.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，三遷為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, after three promotions he was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Zhou was eventually appointed Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 到官，系囚數百。

translations.literal: On reaching office, several hundred prisoners were held.
translations.idiomatic: When he took office, several hundred prisoners awaited judgment.

sentences.zh: 胄剖斷旬日便了，囹圄空虛。

translations.literal: Zhou judged and decided in ten days and finished; the prisons were empty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou cleared the docket within ten days, and the prisons stood empty.

sentences.zh: 有陳州人向道力偽作高平郡守，將之官。

translations.literal: A man of Chenzhou, Xiang Daoli, forged credentials as Administrator of Gaoping Commandery and was going to take office.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Chenzhou named Xiang Daoli forged credentials as Administrator of Gaoping and was on his way to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 胄遇諸塗，察其有異，將留詰之。

translations.literal: Zhou met him on the road, perceived something strange, and was about to detain and question him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou met him on the road, sensed something amiss, and was about to detain him for questioning.

sentences.zh: 司馬王君馥固諫，乃聽詣郡。

translations.literal: The Major Wang Junfu strongly remonstrated, and he was allowed to go to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Major Wang Junfu strongly objected, and Zhou allowed the man to proceed to his post.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，即遣主簿追道力。

translations.literal: Soon he regretted it and at once sent the registrar to pursue Daoli.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted this and sent his registrar to pursue Daoli.

sentences.zh: 有部人徐俱羅嘗任海陵郡守，先是已為道力偽代之。

translations.literal: A subordinate, Xu Juluo, had once served as Administrator of Hailing Commandery and had already been falsely replaced by Daoli.
translations.idiomatic: A subordinate named Xu Juluo had once served as Administrator of Hailing and had already been supplanted by Daoli's imposture.

sentences.zh: 比至秩滿，公私不悟。

translations.literal: By the time his term ended, neither public nor private parties had realized it.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the term ended, neither the court nor the local authorities had noticed the fraud.

sentences.zh: 俱羅遂語君馥曰：「向道力經賜代為郡，使君豈容疑之。

translations.literal: Juluo then said to Junfu: "Xiang Daoli was long ago granted to replace me in the commandery—how can the envoy allow suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: Juluo told Junfu, "Xiang Daoli was officially appointed to replace me—how can you doubt him?

sentences.zh: 」君馥以俱羅所陳，又固請胄。

translations.literal: " Junfu, based on what Juluo stated, again strongly urged Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Junfu, citing Juluo's account, again pressed Zhou to drop the matter.

sentences.zh: 胄呵，君馥乃止。

translations.literal: Zhou shouted at him and Junfu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou rebuked him sharply, and Junfu desisted.

sentences.zh: 遂收之，道力懼而引偽。

translations.literal: He then arrested him; Daoli in fear confessed the forgery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had him arrested, and Daoli, in fear, confessed the imposture.

sentences.zh: 其發奸擿伏，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His exposing treachery and uncovering hidden wrongs were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His exposure of fraud and hidden crime was always of this sort.

sentences.zh: 時人謂為神明，先是，兗州城東沂、泗二水合而南流，氾濫大澤中。

translations.literal: People of the time called him divine; earlier, east of Yanzhou city the Yi and Si rivers joined and flowed south, flooding a great marsh.
translations.idiomatic: People called him uncannily perceptive. East of Yanzhou the Yi and Si rivers had joined and flowed south, flooding a great marsh.

sentences.zh: 胄遂積石堰之，決令西注，陂澤盡為良田。

translations.literal: Zhou then piled stone to dam them, cut a channel westward, and the marshes all became good fields.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou built stone dams, diverted the water westward, and turned the marshes into fertile farmland.

sentences.zh: 又通轉運，利盡淮海，百姓賴之，號為薛公豐兗渠。

translations.literal: He also opened transport routes, profit extending throughout Huai and Hai; the people relied on it, calling it Duke Xue's Abundant Yanzhou Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened transport routes that benefited the whole Huai-Hai region; the people called it Duke Xue's Abundant Yanzhou Canal.

sentences.zh: 胄以天下太平，遂遣博士登泰山觀古跡，撰封禪圖及儀上之。

translations.literal: Zhou, because the realm was at peace, then sent a scholar to ascend Mount Tai to view ancient traces, composed diagrams and rites for the Feng and Shan sacrifices, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Believing the realm was at peace, Zhou sent a scholar to Mount Tai to survey ancient sites and submitted plans and rites for a Feng and Shan ceremony.

sentences.zh: 帝謙讓不許。

translations.literal: The emperor modestly declined and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor modestly declined.

sentences.zh: 轉郢州刺史，有惠政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Yingzhou and had benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Inspector of Yingzhou, he governed with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 徵拜衛尉卿，轉大理卿，持法寬平，名為稱職。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of the Guards, transferred to Minister of Justice; he held the law leniently and evenly and was named as fulfilling his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Minister of the Guards and then Minister of Justice, he applied the law with leniency and fairness and won a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was moved to Director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射高熲稍被疏忌，及王世積誅，熲事與相連，上因此欲成熲罪。

translations.literal: At that time the Left Vice Director Gao Jiong was gradually distanced and suspected; when Wang Shiji was executed, Jiong's affair was connected, and the emperor therefore wished to complete Jiong's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Gao Jiong had fallen under suspicion; when Wang Shiji was executed, Jiong was implicated, and the emperor sought grounds to convict him.

sentences.zh: 胄明雪之，正議其獄。

translations.literal: Zhou clearly cleared him and properly judged his case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou cleared him and judged the case on its merits.

sentences.zh: 由是忤旨，械系之，久而得免。

translations.literal: Thereby he offended the imperial will; he was shackled and imprisoned, and after a long time obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: This defiance of the emperor's will led to his shackling and imprisonment; he was released only after a long interval.

sentences.zh: 檢校相州事，甚有能名。

translations.literal: He was made to inspect and oversee Xiangzhou affairs and had a great reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed to oversee Xiangzhou, he earned a strong reputation for administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒作亂并州，遣其將綦良東略地，攻逼慈州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Han, Yang Liang, rebelled in Bingzhou, sent his general Qi Liang east to seize territory, and attacked and pressed Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Han, Yang Liang, rebelled in Bingzhou, he sent his general Qi Liang east to seize territory and pressed the attack on Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史上官政請援於胄，胄畏諒兵鋒，不敢拒。

translations.literal: The Prefect Shangguan Zheng requested aid from Zhou; Zhou feared Liang's military edge and did not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Shangguan Zheng asked Zhou for help; Zhou, fearing Liang's military momentum, did not dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 良又引兵攻胄，胄欲以計卻之，遣親人魯世范說良曰：「天下事未可知。

translations.literal: Liang again led troops to attack Zhou; Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to persuade Liang, saying: "The outcome of affairs under Heaven is not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: Liang marched on Zhou again; Zhou hoped to drive him off by stratagem and sent his confidant Lu Shifan to say to Liang, "The outcome of affairs under Heaven is still uncertain.

sentences.zh: 胄為人臣，去就須得其所，何遽相攻也？

translations.literal: Zhou is a subject—his going and staying must find their proper place; why attack each other so hastily?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou is a subject; where he stands or withdraws must be chosen rightly—why press the attack so soon?

sentences.zh: 」良乃釋去，進圍黎陽。

translations.literal: " Liang then released him and advanced to besiege Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang then withdrew and marched on to besiege Liyang.

sentences.zh: 及良為史祥所攻，棄軍歸胄。

translations.literal: When Liang was attacked by Shi Xiang, he abandoned his army and returned to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xiang attacked Liang, Liang abandoned his forces and fled back to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以胄懷貳心，鎖詣大理。

translations.literal: The court, judging that Zhou harbored a divided heart, shackled him and sent him to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The court suspected Zhou of divided loyalty, put him in chains, and sent him to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 相州吏人素懷其恩，詣闕理胄者百餘人。

translations.literal: The officials and people of Xiangzhou, who long cherished his kindness, numbered over a hundred in going to the capital to plead for Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred officials and commoners of Xiangzhou, who had long benefited from his kindness, went to the capital to plead on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 胄竟坐除名，配防嶺南，道卒。

translations.literal: Zhou in the end was punished by removal from the register, assigned to guard the Lingnan frontier, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was finally stripped of office, sent to serve on the Lingnan frontier, and died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 子筠、獻知名。

translations.literal: His sons Yun and Xian became well known.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yun and Xian won renown.

sentences.zh: 端弟裕，字仁友。

translations.literal: Duan's younger brother Yu, styled Renyou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan's younger brother Yu, styled Renyou.

sentences.zh: 少以孝悌聞於州裏。

translations.literal: In youth he was known in the district for filial piety and brotherly love.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known throughout the district for filial piety and brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，丞相參軍事。

translations.literal: At twenty he served as an aide in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he became an aide in the Chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 時京兆韋夐志安放逸，不幹世務。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Juan of Jingzhao aspired to seclusion and ease and did not engage in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Juan of Jingzhao sought a life of seclusion and ease and kept out of public affairs.

sentences.zh: 裕慕其恬靜，數載酒肴侯之，談宴終日。

translations.literal: Yu admired his tranquillity, repeatedly carried wine and food to wait on him, and talked and feasted all day.
translations.idiomatic: Yu admired his quiet manner, often brought wine and food to visit him, and they would talk and feast the day through.

sentences.zh: 夐遂以從孫女妻之。

translations.literal: Juan then gave him his grand-niece in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Juan then gave Yu his grand-niece in marriage.

sentences.zh: 裕嘗謂親友曰：「大丈夫當聖明之運，而無灼然文武之用為世所知，雖復棲遑，徙為勞苦耳。

translations.literal: Yu once told kin and friends: "When a great man meets an age of sage illumination yet lacks clear civil and military attainments known to the world, even if he wanders in restlessness it is only wasted toil.
translations.idiomatic: Yu once told relatives and friends, "A man ought to live in an age of enlightened rule, yet if he lacks unmistakable civil or military gifts that the world recognizes, even restless wandering is only wasted hardship.

sentences.zh: 至如韋居士，退不丘壑，進不市朝，怡然守道，榮辱弗及，何其樂也。」

translations.literal: As for Master Wei the recluse—in retirement he does not hide in mountain ravines, in advancement he does not court the marketplace; he guards the Way with ease, glory and disgrace do not reach him—how joyous!"
translations.idiomatic: Take Master Wei: in withdrawal he does not bury himself in ravines, in advancement he does not chase the court; he keeps the Way with ease, untouched by honor or shame—what joy is that!"

sentences.zh: 裕曾宿宴於夐之廬，後庭有井，裕夜出戶，若有人欲牽其手，裕便卻行，遂落井。

translations.literal: Yu once lodged for a banquet at Juan's hut; there was a well in the rear courtyard. Yu went out at night; it seemed someone wished to take his hand; Yu stepped back and fell into the well.
translations.idiomatic: Yu once stayed for a feast at Juan's cottage, where there was a well in the back court. He went out at night and felt as if someone were pulling his hand; he stepped back and fell into the well.

sentences.zh: 同坐共出之，因勸裕酒曰：「向慮卿不測夐，幸得無他，宜盡此爵。

translations.literal: Those seated together pulled him out and urged wine on Yu, saying: "Just now I feared you might meet mischance from Juan's place; fortunately there was no harm—you should drain this cup.
translations.idiomatic: His companions pulled him out and pressed him to drink, saying, "I feared something untoward might come from Juan's house; luckily you are unhurt—you should finish this cup.

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「墜井蓋小小耳，方當逾於此也。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Falling in a well is a small matter; something greater is yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu said, "A fall into a well is a small thing; something worse lies ahead.

sentences.zh: 」人問其故，裕曰：「近夢，恐有兩楹之憂。

translations.literal: " When people asked the reason, Yu said: "A dream lately—I fear there may be the grief of 'two pillars.'
translations.idiomatic: " Asked why, he said, "I dreamed recently and fear the omen of 'two pillars.'

sentences.zh: 」尋卒，文章之士誄之者數人。

translations.literal: " Soon after he died; several literary men composed dirges for him.
translations.idiomatic: " He died soon after, and several men of letters wrote dirges for him.

sentences.zh: 周文傷惜之，追贈洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen mourned and cherished his memory and posthumously enfeoffed him as Inspector of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen grieved for him and posthumously appointed him Inspector of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 胄從祖弟浚，字道賾。

translations.literal: Zhou's first cousin once removed Jun, styled Daoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's first cousin once removed, Xue Jun, styled Daoyin.

sentences.zh: 父琰，周渭南太守。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Administrator of Weinan under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had served as Administrator of Weinan under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 浚少孤，養母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jun lost his father young; he nourished his mother and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was orphaned young; he supported his mother and became famed for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，有志行。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and had resolve and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning and showed firm character.

sentences.zh: 周天和中，襲爵虞城侯，位新豐令。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era of Northern Zhou he inherited the marquisate of Yucheng and held the post of Magistrate of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: During Northern Zhou's Tianhe reign he inherited the marquisate of Yucheng and served as Magistrate of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 隨開皇中，曆尚書虞部、考功侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he successively served in the Ministry of Works, Bureau of Parks and Forests, and as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui's Kaihuang reign he rose through posts in the Ministry of Works and as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝聞浚事母孝，以其母老，賜輿服几杖、四時珍味，當世榮之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Jun was filial toward his mother; because his mother was old, he bestowed carriage robes, cane and armrest, and delicacies for the four seasons—the age honored this.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of Jun's devotion to his mother, he granted her carriage robes, a cane and armrest, and seasonal delicacies—a mark of honor the age admired.

sentences.zh: 後其母疾病，浚貌甚憂瘁，親故弗之識。

translations.literal: Later when his mother fell ill, Jun's appearance was deeply haggard with worry; kin and friends did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother later fell ill, Jun grew so haggard with grief that friends and kin scarcely knew him.

sentences.zh: 暨丁母艱，詔鴻臚監護喪事，歸葬夏陽。

translations.literal: When he completed mourning for his mother, an edict ordered the Grand Herald to supervise the funeral and he returned to bury her at Xiayang.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering mourning for his mother, he was ordered to have the Grand Herald supervise the funeral and returned to bury her at Xiayang.

sentences.zh: 時隆冬極寒，浚衰絰徙跣，冒犯霜雪，自京及鄉，五百餘里，足凍墮指，創血流離，朝野為之傷痛。

translations.literal: It was deep winter and extreme cold; Jun in mourning weeds went barefoot, braving frost and snow from the capital to his home village, over five hundred li; his feet froze and toes fell off, wounds bleeding and flowing—court and countryside were pained for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the depths of winter he went barefoot in mourning garb through frost and snow for more than five hundred li from the capital to his home; his feet froze, toes fell off, and blood streamed from his wounds—the court and the people were stricken with grief.

sentences.zh: 州裏賵助，一無所受。

translations.literal: Condolence gifts from the district—he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted none of the condolence gifts offered by the district.

sentences.zh: 尋起令視事，上見其毀瘠過甚，為之改容，顧群臣曰：「吾見薛濬哀毀，不覺悲感傷懷。」嗟異久之。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to resume office as magistrate. The emperor, seeing him emaciated beyond measure, changed expression and told the assembled ministers: "When I see Xue Jun's grieving devastation, I cannot but feel grief wound my breast." He sighed in wonder for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to office. The emperor, struck by his wasted frame, changed countenance and told the ministers, "Seeing Xue Jun's mourning ruin, I cannot keep grief from wounding my heart." He sighed in admiration for a long while.

sentences.zh: 浚竟不勝喪，病且卒。

translations.literal: Jun in the end could not overcome his mourning; he fell ill and was about to die.
translations.idiomatic: Jun could not bear the mourning in the end; he fell ill and was near death.

sentences.zh: 其弟謨時為晉王府兵曹參軍事，在揚州。濬遺書於謨曰：

translations.literal: His younger brother Mo at the time was an aide in the Prince of Jin's military affairs office, in Yangzhou. Jun left a testamentary letter to Mo, saying:
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mo was then serving on the staff of the Prince of Jin's military office in Yangzhou. Jun wrote a final letter to Mo:

sentences.zh: 吾以不造，幼丁艱酷，窮遊約處，屢絕簞瓢。

translations.literal: I have been ill-fated; in youth I encountered bitter hardship, wandering in poverty and narrow circumstances, often without even a basket of rice.
translations.idiomatic: I have been ill-fated; in youth I suffered bitter hardship, living in poverty and want, often without even a meal in my basket.

sentences.zh: 晚生早孤，不聞《詩禮》。

translations.literal: Born late and orphaned early, I never heard the Odes and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Born late and orphaned young, I never properly learned the Odes and Rites.

sentences.zh: 賴奉先人貽厥之訓，獲稟母氏聖善之規。

translations.literal: I relied on my forebears' bequeathed instruction and received my mother's sage and good teaching.
translations.idiomatic: I had my ancestors' bequeathed teaching and my mother's wise and gentle guidance.

sentences.zh: 負笈裹糧，不憚艱遠，從師就業，欲罷不能。

translations.literal: Carrying books on my back and provisions wrapped, not fearing hardship and distance, I followed teachers to pursue learning, wishing to stop yet unable.
translations.idiomatic: I carried books on my back and bundled provisions, unafraid of hardship and distance, followed teachers to study, and could not bring myself to stop.

sentences.zh: 砥行礪心，困而彌篤，用膺教義，爰至長成。

translations.literal: Polishing conduct and tempering the heart, growing more steadfast in adversity, I thereby received their teaching until full growth.
translations.idiomatic: I tempered conduct and heart, growing firmer through hardship, and so received their teaching until I came of age.

sentences.zh: 自釋耒登朝，於茲二十三年矣。

translations.literal: Since I laid down the plough and entered court service, twenty-three years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Since I left the fields for office, twenty-three years have now passed.

sentences.zh: 雖官非聞達，而祿喜逮親，庶保期頤，得終色養。

translations.literal: Although my office was not eminent, my salary was glad to reach my parent; I hoped to secure full years and end my days in providing for her comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Though my rank was not lofty, my salary at least reached my mother; I hoped to live out a full span and care for her to the end.

sentences.zh: 何圖精誠無感，禍酷薦臻；

translations.literal: Who could have thought that utmost sincerity would move nothing, and bitter calamity would come in succession?
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that deepest devotion would win no response, and crushing misfortune would follow one upon another?

sentences.zh: 兄弟俱被奪情，苦廬靡申哀訴。

translations.literal: Both brothers were stripped of mourning leave; in bitter hut-dwelling we could not voice our grief.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers were forced from mourning; in our rough shelters we could not even voice our grief.

sentences.zh: 是用叩心泣血，隕氣摧魂者也。

translations.literal: For this reason I beat my heart and weep blood; my breath falls away and my spirit is broken.
translations.idiomatic: That is why my heart is torn and my spirit broken.

sentences.zh: 既而創钜釁深，不勝荼毒，啟手啟足，幸及全歸。

translations.literal: Then wounds were great and guilt ran deep; I could not bear the bitter torment. Opening my hands and feet, I am fortunate to attain a whole return.
translations.idiomatic: Then my wounds grew grave beyond bearing; I open my limbs in the hope of dying whole.

sentences.zh: 使夫死而有知，得從先人於地下矣，豈非至願哉？

translations.literal: If the dead have awareness, to follow my forebears in the nether world—would that not be my utmost wish?
translations.idiomatic: If the dead retain awareness, to join my ancestors beneath the earth—what greater wish could there be?

sentences.zh: 但念爾伶俜孤宦，遠在邊服，顧此悢悢，如何可言！

translations.literal: Yet I think of you, solitary in office far away on the frontier; facing this anguish, what can be said!
translations.idiomatic: Yet I think of you alone in a distant post on the frontier; at this sorrow, what words are enough!

sentences.zh: 適已有書，冀得與汝面訣，忍死待汝，已曆一旬。

translations.literal: I have just sent a letter, hoping to take leave of you face to face; I endure death waiting for you—it has already been ten days.
translations.idiomatic: I wrote again hoping to see you once more; I have clung to life waiting for you these ten days already.

sentences.zh: 汝既未來，便成今古，緬然永別，為恨何言！

translations.literal: You have not come; past and present are fixed—afar we part forever; what regret can words express!
translations.idiomatic: You did not come; what was possible is now past; this distant farewell—what words can measure the regret!

sentences.zh: 勉之哉！

translations.literal: Strive on!
translations.idiomatic: Take heart!

sentences.zh: 勉之哉！

translations.literal: Strive on!
translations.idiomatic: Take heart!

sentences.zh: 勉之哉！

translations.literal: Strive on!
translations.idiomatic: Take heart!

sentences.zh: 書成而絕。

translations.literal: When the letter was finished he died.
translations.idiomatic: He finished the letter and died.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，文帝為之屑涕，降使齎冊書弔祭。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported it; Emperor Wen shed tears for him and sent down an envoy bearing patent documents for condolence and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported his death; Emperor Wen wept and sent an envoy with imperial documents of condolence and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 浚性清儉，死日家無遺財。

translations.literal: Jun by nature was pure and frugal; on the day of his death the household had no property left.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was by nature austere and frugal; when he died his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 浚初為兒時，與宗中兒戲澗濱，見一黃蛇，有角及足。

translations.literal: When Jun was first a child, he played with boys of the clan by a stream and saw a yellow serpent with horns and feet.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Jun played with kinsmen's children by a stream and saw a yellow serpent with horns and feet.

sentences.zh: 召群童共視，了無見者。

translations.literal: He called the group of children to look together; none at all saw it.
translations.idiomatic: He called the other boys to look, but none of them could see it.

sentences.zh: 以為不祥，歸大憂悴。

translations.literal: He took it as inauspicious and returned in great distress and dejection.
translations.idiomatic: He took it as an ill omen and went home deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 母問之，以實對。

translations.literal: His mother asked him and he answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother asked, he told her what had happened.

sentences.zh: 時有胡僧詣宅乞食，母以告之。

translations.literal: At that time a foreign monk came to the house to beg food; the mother told him of it.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk came to the house begging food, and his mother told him the story.

sentences.zh: 僧曰：「此兒之吉應。

translations.literal: The monk said: "This is the boy's auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: The monk said, "This is an auspicious sign for the boy.

sentences.zh: 且此兒早有名位，然壽不過六七耳。

translations.literal: Moreover this boy will early attain name and rank, yet his years will not exceed six or seven tens."
translations.idiomatic: He will win fame and office early, yet his life will not pass sixty or seventy."

sentences.zh: 」言終而出，忽然不見。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking he went out and suddenly was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he left and vanished abruptly.

sentences.zh: 後終於四十二，六七之言驗矣。

translations.literal: Later he died at forty-two—the words about six or seven tens were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at forty-two, and the prophecy of "six or seven tens" was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 子乾福，武安郡司倉書佐。

translations.literal: His son Qianfu was a clerical aide in the granary office of Wu'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianfu served as a clerical aide in the granary office of Wu'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 洪隆弟湖，字破胡。

translations.literal: Honglong's younger brother Hu, styled Pohu.
translations.idiomatic: Honglong's younger brother Hu, styled Pohu.

sentences.zh: 少有節操，篤志於學；

translations.literal: From youth he had moral discipline and devoted his will to learning;
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed moral discipline and devoted himself to learning;

sentences.zh: 專精講習，不幹時務；

translations.literal: he specialized in lecturing and study and did not meddle in current affairs;
translations.idiomatic: he specialized in teaching and study and kept out of worldly affairs;

sentences.zh: 與物無競，好以德義服人。

translations.literal: he did not contend with others and liked to win people through virtue and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: he did not strive with others and preferred to win people through virtue and integrity.

sentences.zh: 或有兄弟忿鬩，鄰里爭訟者，恐湖聞之，皆內自改悔。

translations.literal: When brothers quarreled in anger or neighbors had lawsuits, fearing Hu might hear, all inwardly repented and changed.
translations.idiomatic: If brothers quarreled or neighbors went to law, they feared Hu might hear and would repent on their own.

sentences.zh: 鄉閭化其風教，咸以敬讓為先。

translations.literal: Villages and lanes were transformed by his teaching; all took respect and yielding as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: The countryside was shaped by his example; everyone put respect and forbearance first.

sentences.zh: 三召州都，再辟主簿，州將傾心致禮，並不獲己而應之。

translations.literal: Three times summoned as district chief, twice recruited as registrar—the prefect gave him his full heart in courtesy, and in each case he responded only because he could not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: He was thrice summoned as district chief and twice offered the post of registrar; the prefect treated him with full respect, and each time he accepted only because he could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 為本州中從事、別駕、除河東太守。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant of this province, Vice Director, and was appointed Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as provincial attendant and vice director, then was appointed Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並為本郡，當世榮之。

translations.literal: Brothers together held office in their home commandery—the age honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers holding office together in their home commandery was the envy of the age.

sentences.zh: 復受詔為仇池都將。

translations.literal: He again received an edict as Commander-in-chief of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed by edict as commander of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 後罷郡，終於家。

translations.literal: Later he left the commandery and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later left office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 有八子，長子聰知名。

translations.literal: He had eight sons; the eldest, Cong, became well known.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons; the eldest, Cong, won renown.

sentences.zh: 聰字延智。

translations.literal: Cong, styled Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, styled Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 方正有理識，善自標緻，不妄遊處。

translations.literal: Upright and square, he had reason and discernment, was good at setting his own standard, and did not wander or lodge rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and discerning, he held himself to a strict standard and did not roam or socialize lightly.

sentences.zh: 雖在暗室，終日矜莊，見者莫不懍然加敬。

translations.literal: Even in a dark room he remained dignified and grave all day; those who saw him none failed to feel awe and add respect.
translations.idiomatic: Even alone in a dark room he remained grave and composed all day; all who met him were moved to reverence.

sentences.zh: 博覽墳籍，精力過人，至於前言往行，多所究悉。
