translations.literal: He broadly perused the classics, his energy surpassing others; as for words and deeds of former ages, he investigated and understood many.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and had unusual stamina; he studied deeply the words and deeds of past ages.

sentences.zh: 詞辯占對，尤是所長。

translations.literal: Rhetoric, disputation, and responsive exchange were especially his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Debate and repartee were his particular strengths.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，廬於墓側，哭泣之聲，酸感行路。

translations.literal: When he encountered his father's mourning, he built a hut beside the tomb; the sound of his weeping bitterly moved passers-by on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he dwelt in a hut by the tomb; his weeping moved all who passed on the road.

sentences.zh: 友于篤睦，而家教甚嚴；

translations.literal: He was deeply affectionate with his brothers, yet family teaching was very strict;
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his brothers, yet household discipline was severe;

sentences.zh: 諸弟雖昏宦，恆不免杖罰，對之肅如也。

translations.literal: the younger brothers, though married and in office, constantly could not escape beating with the staff; toward him they were reverent as before a superior.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brothers, though married and in office, were still liable to the rod; in his presence they were always deferential.

sentences.zh: 未弱冠，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: Before the cap and girdle at twenty, the province recruited him as registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age the province appointed him registrar.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年，釋褐著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he doffed commoner's cloth and became Assistant in the Office for Compiling Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he entered office as Assistant in the Office for Compiling Literature.

sentences.zh: 于時，孝文留心氏族，正定官品。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowen attended to clans and families and fixed official ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xiaowen was reforming the clans and fixing official ranks.

sentences.zh: 士大夫解巾，優者不過奉朝請。

translations.literal: When scholar-officials removed their headcloth, the best among them rose no higher than Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: When gentlemen entered service, even the best rarely rose above Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 聰起家便佐著作，時論美之。

translations.literal: Cong at the start of his career was at once assistant in the compiling office—opinion of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Cong began his career directly as an assistant in the compiling office, which contemporaries praised.

sentences.zh: 後遷書侍御史，凡所彈劾，不避強禦；

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Attending Censor; in all impeachments he did not avoid the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Attending Censor and in every impeachment refused to spare the powerful.

sentences.zh: 孝文或欲寬貸者，聰輒爭之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen sometimes wished to show leniency, Cong always contested it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Xiaowen wished to show leniency, Cong argued against it.

sentences.zh: 帝每云：「朕見薛聰，不能不憚，何況諸人也？

translations.literal: The emperor often said: "When I see Xue Cong I cannot but feel awe—how much more other people?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said, "When I see Xue Cong I cannot help but feel awe—how much more so for others?

sentences.zh: 」自是貴戚斂手。

translations.literal: " From this the noble kin restrained their hands.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on the imperial kin held themselves in check.

sentences.zh: 累遷直閣將軍，兼給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍，直閣如故。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he reached Direct Gate General, concurrently Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Roving Cavalier Attendant; the Direct Gate post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Direct Gate General and was concurrently appointed Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Roving Cavalier Attendant, while retaining his Direct Gate position.

sentences.zh: 聰深為孝文所知，外以德器遇之，內以心膂為寄。

translations.literal: Cong was deeply known to Emperor Xiaowen; outwardly he was met with virtue and capacity, inwardly entrusted as backbone and flank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen knew him well: outwardly he honored his character and ability, inwardly he entrusted him as a core adviser.

sentences.zh: 親衛禁兵，委總管領。

translations.literal: The close guard and forbidden troops he entrusted to [Cong's] overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He placed the imperial guard under Cong's command.

sentences.zh: 故終太和之世，恆帶直閣將軍。

translations.literal: Therefore through the Tahe era he constantly bore the title Direct Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Tahe reign he therefore always held the title of Direct Gate General.

sentences.zh: 群臣罷朝之後，聰恆陪侍帷幄，言兼晝夜。

translations.literal: After the ministers left court, Cong always attended beside the curtained throne, speech spanning day and night.
translations.idiomatic: After court was dismissed, Cong invariably remained at the emperor's side, and their counsel could run from day into night.

sentences.zh: 時政得失，預以謀謨；

translations.literal: The gains and losses of current policy—he took part in counsel and planning;
translations.idiomatic: He took part in planning on the rights and wrongs of current policy;

sentences.zh: 動輒匡諫，事多聽允。

translations.literal: He repeatedly corrected and remonstrated; affairs mostly received approval.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated again and again, and the emperor mostly heeded him.

sentences.zh: 而重厚沈密，外莫窺其際。

translations.literal: Yet he was weighty, thick, deep, and sealed—outsiders could not peer into his inner ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was grave and reserved; outsiders could not fathom his inner mind.

sentences.zh: 帝欲進以名位，輒苦讓不受。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to advance him in titles and ranks; he always bitterly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to promote him in rank and title, he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 帝亦雅相體悉，謂之曰：「卿天爵自高，固非人爵之所榮也。

translations.literal: The emperor also by refinement mutually understood him fully, saying to him: "Your heavenly rank is itself lofty—solidly it is not what human ranks can honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood him perfectly and said, "Your innate nobility is too high to be honored by mere human titles.

sentences.zh: 」又除羽林監。

translations.literal: " He was again appointed Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝曾與朝臣論海內姓地人物，戲謂聰曰：「世人謂卿諸薛是蜀人，定是蜀人不？

translations.literal: The emperor once with court ministers discussed surnames, places, and persons within the realm; in jest he said to Cong: "People say your branch of Xue are Shu men—is that certainly so?
translations.idiomatic: Once, while discussing leading families and figures across the realm with his ministers, the emperor jokingly asked Cong, "People say your Xue clan are Shu men—are you Shu men or not?

sentences.zh: 」聰對曰：「臣遠祖廣德，世仕漢朝，時人呼為漢。

translations.literal: " Cong replied: "Your servant's distant ancestor Guangde served the Han court for generations; men of the time called them Han.
translations.idiomatic: Cong answered, "My distant ancestor Guangde served the Han dynasty for generations, and people called us Han.

sentences.zh: 臣九世祖永，隨劉備入蜀，時人呼為蜀。

translations.literal: Your servant's ninth-generation ancestor Yong followed Liu Bei into Shu; men of the time called them Shu.
translations.idiomatic: My ninth-generation ancestor Yong followed Liu Bei into Shu, and people called us Shu.

sentences.zh: 臣今事陛下，是虜非蜀也。

translations.literal: Your servant now serves Your Majesty—it is captive [northern] state, not Shu.
translations.idiomatic: I now serve Your Majesty—we are northerners, not Shu.

sentences.zh: 」帝撫掌笑曰：「卿幸可自明非蜀，何乃遂復苦朕。

translations.literal: " The emperor clapped his hands and laughed, saying: "You could fortunately clarify yourself as not Shu—why then must you again distress me?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor clapped his hands and laughed. "You could have simply said you are not Shu—why must you torment me again?

sentences.zh: 」聰因投戟而出。

translations.literal: " Cong thereupon cast down his halberd and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Cong threw down his halberd and stalked out.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「薛監醉耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Supervisor Xue is merely drunk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Supervisor Xue is merely drunk.

sentences.zh: 」其見知如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the degree of his being known and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of the emperor's regard for him.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，從駕南征，兼御史中尉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he followed the imperial procession on the southern campaign, concurrently Central Commander of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign and was made concurrent Central Commander of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 及宣武即位，除都督、齊州刺史，政存簡靜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne, [Cong] was appointed Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Qizhou; his governance preserved simplicity and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu succeeded to the throne, Cong was appointed regional commander and Governor of Qizhou, governing with simplicity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 卒於州，吏人追思，留其所坐榻以存遺愛。

translations.literal: He died in the province; officials and people cherished his memory and kept the couch on which he had sat to preserve his lingering affection.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; officials and commoners mourned him and preserved the couch where he had sat as a token of his kindness.

sentences.zh: 贈征虜將軍、華州刺史，諡曰簡懿侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Huazhou; posthumous title Marquis Jianyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Huazhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Jianyi.

sentences.zh: 魏前二年，重贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、延州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year before Wei [ended], he was again posthumously awarded Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Two years before the fall of Wei, he was again posthumously honored as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and as Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 子孝通最知名。

translations.literal: His son Xiaotong was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaotong was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 孝通字士達。

translations.literal: Xiaotong, styled Shida.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong, styled Shida.

sentences.zh: 博學有俊才。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, with outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and possessed outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤征關中，引參驃騎大將軍府事，禮遇甚隆。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned in Guanzhong, he brought [Xiaotong] in to assist the Rapid Cavalry Grand General's headquarters affairs; courtesy and treatment were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned in Guanzhong, he brought Xiaotong into his staff at the Rapid Cavalry Grand General's headquarters and treated him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤將有異志，孝通悟其萌，托以拜掃求歸，乃見許。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was about to harbor divergent intent, Xiaotong perceived its sprouting; on the pretext of tomb-sweeping he sought to return home, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was plotting rebellion, Xiaotong sensed it early and asked leave to return home on the pretext of tending ancestral graves; his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 同寮咸怪，止之；

translations.literal: Colleagues all found it strange and tried to stop him;
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues were astonished and tried to stop him;

sentences.zh: 但笑而不答，遽還鄉里。

translations.literal: he only smiled and did not answer, and swiftly returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: but he only smiled and said nothing, and hurried home.

sentences.zh: 寶夤後果逆命。

translations.literal: Baoyin afterward indeed rebelled against orders.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin did rebel, as Xiaotong had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 北海王元顥入洛，宗人薛永宗、修義等又聚徙作亂，欲以應之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, entered Luoyang; clansmen Xue Yongzong, Xiuyi, and others again gathered displaced people in revolt, wishing to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, entered Luoyang, clansmen Xue Yongzong and Xiuyi raised armed bands among displaced people to join him.

sentences.zh: 孝通與所親計曰：「北海乘虛遠入，吳兵不能久住，事必無成。

translations.literal: Xiaotong consulted with those close to him, saying: "Beihai rides vacancy and enters from afar; Wu troops cannot long remain—the affair is bound to fail.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong told his intimates, "The Prince of Beihai has seized a moment of weakness to march in from afar; Liang troops cannot hold Luoyang—the enterprise must fail.

sentences.zh: 今若與永宗等舉，滅族道也。

translations.literal: Now if we join Yongzong and the rest in rising, the road is extinction of the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: If we join Yongzong now, we walk our clan to extinction.

sentences.zh: 」乃率其近親，與河東太守元襲嬰城固守。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led his nearest kin, and with Hedong Governor Yuan Xi held the city in desperate defense.
translations.idiomatic: " He led his close kin and, with Hedong governor Yuan Xi, held the city in a desperate defense.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤平定，元顥退走，預其事者咸罹禍，唯同孝通者皆免。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was pacified and Yuan Hao retreated, all who took part in the affair suffered calamity; only those who acted like Xiaotong were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was crushed and Yuan Hao fled, all who had joined the revolt were ruined—only those who had followed Xiaotong's course were spared.

sentences.zh: 事寧，入洛，除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he entered Luoyang and was appointed Outside-the-Number Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was restored he went to Luoyang and was appointed Outside-the-Number Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 爾硃天光鎮關右，表為關西大行台郎中，深見任遇。

translations.literal: Erzhu Tianguang held Guanzhong; [Xiaotong] was recommended as Registrar of the Guanxi Grand Commissioner and deeply trusted and favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang held Guanzhong, Xiaotong was recommended as registrar on the Guanxi Grand Commissioner's staff and won his deep trust.

sentences.zh: 關中平定，預有其力，以功賜爵汾陰侯。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong was pacified he had a share in the achievement; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: He played a part in pacifying Guanzhong and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fenyin for his service.

sentences.zh: 莊帝既幽崩，元曄地又疏遠，更議主社稷。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang having died in imprisonment, Yuan Ye's lineage was also remote—they debated anew who should head the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuang died in confinement and Yuan Ye's claim was too remote, the court debated anew who should rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 孝通以廣陵王恭，高祖猶子，又在茂親，夙有令望。

translations.literal: Xiaotong took Prince of Guangling Gong—a great-grandson of Gaozu, also of eminent close kin, long having fine repute.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong favored Prince of Guangling Gong: a grandson of Emperor Gaozu, of the highest imperial kin, and long held in esteem.

sentences.zh: 不言多載，理必陽瘖。

translations.literal: Though he spoke little over many years, reason demanded it must be feigned muteness.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had scarcely spoken for years, his silence was surely feigned—a sign fit for enthronement.

sentences.zh: 奉以為主，天人允葉。

translations.literal: They installed him as sovereign—Heaven and men alike approved.
translations.idiomatic: They enthroned him, and Heaven and men alike assented.

sentences.zh: 世隆等並以為疑。

translations.literal: Shilong and the rest all harbored doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and others were skeptical.

sentences.zh: 孝通密贊天光察之。

translations.literal: Xiaotong secretly urged Tianguang to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong secretly urged Tianguang to look into it.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王曰：「天何言哉？

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangling said: "What has Heaven to say?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangling said, "What has Heaven to say?

sentences.zh: 」於是定冊，即節閔帝也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the succession was fixed—this was Emperor Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: The succession was settled, and he became Emperor Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 以首創大議，拜銀青光祿大夫、散騎常侍，兼中書舍人，封藍田縣子。

translations.literal: For initiating the great deliberation, he was appointed Silver-Gleaming Light Grand Master, Palace Attendant, concurrent Secretariat Gentleman, and enfeoffed Viscount of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: For leading the deliberation on the succession, he was made Silver-Gleaming Light Grand Master and Palace Attendant, appointed concurrent Secretariat Gentleman, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 孝通求以官贈亡兄景懋，又言己有侯爵，請轉授兄息子舒。

translations.literal: Xiaotong asked to use office to posthumously honor his deceased elder brother Jingmao, and also said he already held a marquisate, requesting to transfer it to his brother's son Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong asked that offices be granted posthumously to his dead brother Jingmao, and since he already held a marquisate, asked to pass it to his brother's son Shu.

sentences.zh: 節閔覽啟傷感，以侯爵既重，不容轉授，乃下詔褒美。

translations.literal: Jiemin reading the memorial was moved; since a marquisate was weighty and could not be transferred, he issued an edict praising [Xiaotong].
translations.idiomatic: Jiemin was moved when he read the memorial; because a marquisate could not be transferred, he issued an edict commending Xiaotong's devotion.

sentences.zh: 特贈景懋撫軍、北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Especially posthumously enfeoffed Jingmao as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of North Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao was specially posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of North Yong.

sentences.zh: 孝通尋遷中書郎，深為節閔所知重。

translations.literal: Xiaotong soon was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman and was deeply known and valued by Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong was soon promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and won Jiemin's deep trust.

sentences.zh: 普泰二年正月乙酉，中書舍人元翽獻酒肴，帝因與元翌及孝通等宴，兼奏弦管，命翽吹笛；

translations.literal: In the first month, day yiyou, of the second year of Putai, Secretariat Gentleman Yuan Hui presented wine and viands; the emperor thereupon banqueted with Yuan Yi and Xiaotong and the rest, also having strings and pipes played, and ordered Hui to blow the flute;
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the first month in the second year of Putai, Secretariat Gentleman Yuan Hui brought wine and food; the emperor feasted with Yuan Yi, Xiaotong, and others, had music played, and ordered Hui to play the flute;

sentences.zh: 帝亦親以和之。

translations.literal: The emperor himself also joined in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor joined in himself.

sentences.zh: 因使元翌等嘲，以酒為韻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had Yuan Yi and the rest exchange taunts, using wine as the rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Yuan Yi and the others trade witty verses, taking wine as the rhyme.

sentences.zh: 孝通曰：「既逢堯舜君，願上萬年壽。

translations.literal: Xiaotong said: "Having met a Yao-Shun ruler, I wish to offer ten thousand years of life.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong said, "Having met a sage ruler like Yao or Shun, I wish Your Majesty ten thousand years of life.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「平生好玄默，慚為萬國首。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "All my life I have loved dark silence; ashamed to be head of ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "All my life I have loved quietude; I am ashamed to stand at the head of all nations.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿所謂壽，豈容徙然！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "What you call longevity—how could it be in vain!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "What you call longevity—how could it be empty words!

sentences.zh: 」便命酌酒賜孝通，仍命更嘲，不得中絕。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered wine poured and bestowed on Xiaotong, and still ordered further witty exchange, not permitting interruption midway.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered wine poured for Xiaotong and commanded another round of couplets without a break.

sentences.zh: 孝通即豎忠為韻。

translations.literal: Xiaotong then set loyalty as the rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong chose loyalty as the next rhyme.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿不忘忠臣之心。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You, sir, do not forget the heart of a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have not forgotten the heart of a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 」翽曰：「聖主臨萬機，享世永無窮。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "The sage lord oversees the myriad mechanisms; his reign without end forever.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui said, "The sage ruler oversees all affairs; may his reign never end.

sentences.zh: 」孝通曰：「豈唯被草木，方亦及昆蟲。

translations.literal: " Xiaotong said: "How is it only grass and trees that are covered—even insects share in it.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaotong said, "Your grace covers not only grass and trees, but even the smallest creatures.

sentences.zh: 」翌曰：「朝賢既濟濟，野苗又芃芃。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Court worthies are already numerous; wild seedlings flourish lush again.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Yi said, "The court is full of worthy men, and the wild fields grow thick with grain.

sentences.zh: 」墼唬骸熬馐繼逵闥潄罎楣煲換犂幀！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Ruler and ministers embody fish and water; writing and cart-tracks make one realm of Hua and Rong.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Minister and sovereign are as fish in water; one script and one track unite Chinese and barbarian realms.

sentences.zh: 斃⑼ㄔ唬骸拔⒊夾徘熹祝鱲我源鴰畭裕俊庇謔保䘏⑼携詰浠唢埽莾獠緯詉轹麖甓腽玻饍鞶閱壁印＜右約騁铴宋錚髗锊慂浚嗉诹萍觥？

translations.literal: Xiaotong said: "This humble servant truly receives thick favor—how may I answer Mount Hua and Mount Song?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong said, "Your humble servant is deeply favored—how can I repay grace as great as Mount Hua and Mount Song?

sentences.zh: br>外兄裴伯茂性豪俊，多所輕忽。

translations.literal: His cousin by marriage Pei Bomao's nature was bold and handsome; he lightly disregarded many.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin by marriage Pei Bomao was bold and gifted, and treated most people with disdain.

sentences.zh: 唯欽賞孝通，每有著述，共參同異。

translations.literal: Only Xiaotong he admired; whenever he had writings, they compared notes on differences.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiaotong did he admire; whenever he wrote, they compared and debated their work.

sentences.zh: 孝通以裴宏放過甚，每謂之曰：「兄以阮籍、嵇康何如管仲、樂毅？

translations.literal: Xiaotong, because Pei was excessively grand and unrestrained, often said to him: "Elder brother, how do Ruan Ji and Ji Kang compare with Guan Zhong and Le Yi?
translations.idiomatic: Finding Pei too unrestrained, Xiaotong often asked him, "Do you rank Ruan Ji and Ji Kang above Guan Zhong and Le Yi?

sentences.zh: 」蓋自許經綸，抑裴傲也。

translations.literal: " This was essentially self-claim to statecraft, checking Pei's arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: " He was asserting his own statesmanship and putting Pei's arrogance in its place.

sentences.zh: 裴笑而不答，宏放自若。

translations.literal: Pei smiled without answering, grand and unrestrained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Pei only smiled and said nothing, as grand and free as ever.

sentences.zh: 屬齊神武起兵河朔，攻陷相州刺史劉誕。

translations.literal: At the time when Qi Shenwu raised troops in Heshuo, capturing Xiangzhou Governor Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan of Northern Qi raised an army in Heshuo and captured Xiangzhou governor Liu Yan,

sentences.zh: 爾硃天光自關中討之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Tianguang marched from Guanzhong to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang marched from Guanzhong to attack him.

sentences.zh: 孝通以關中險固，秦漢舊都，須預謀鎮遏，以為後計。

translations.literal: Xiaotong held that Guanzhong was rugged and secure, the old capital of Qin and Han—one must plan beforehand to garrison and restrain it as a later measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong argued that Guanzhong was rugged, the ancient capital of Qin and Han, and must be secured in advance as a fallback.

sentences.zh: 縱河北失利，猶足據之。

translations.literal: Even if Hebei were lost, it would still suffice to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Hebei were lost, Guanzhong would still be enough to hold.

sentences.zh: 節閔深以為然，問誰可任者。

translations.literal: Jiemin deeply agreed and asked who could be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiemin strongly agreed and asked who could take the post.

sentences.zh: 孝通與賀拔岳同事天光，又與周文帝有舊；

translations.literal: Xiaotong had served Tianguang together with Helü Yue, and also had old ties with the future Zhou founder;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong had worked under Tianguang with Helü Yue and was also old friends with the future founder of Northern Zhou;

sentences.zh: 二人並先在關右，因並推薦之。

translations.literal: Both were already in Guanzhong, so he recommended them together.
translations.idiomatic: both were already in the west, and he recommended them together.

sentences.zh: 乃超授岳岐、華、秦、雍諸軍事，關西大行台，雍州牧。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue was extraordinarily appointed Commander over Qi, Hua, Qin, and Yong, Grand Commissioner of Guanxi, and Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was then given extraordinary command over Qi, Hua, Qin, and Yong, made Grand Commissioner of Guanxi, and appointed Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 周文帝為左丞，孝通為右丞。

translations.literal: The future Zhou founder served as Left Vice-Director, Xiaotong as Right Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: The future Zhou founder was made left vice-director and Xiaotong right vice-director.

sentences.zh: 齎詔書馳驛入關授嶽等，同鎮長安。

translations.literal: Bearing the edict they raced post-horses into Guanzhong to invest Yue and the rest, jointly garrisoning Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: They carried the edict by post-horse into Guanzhong to invest Yue and his colleagues, and together garrisoned Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 嶽深相器重，待以師友之禮。

translations.literal: Yue deeply valued and trusted him, treating him with rites due teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Yue held him in the highest regard and treated him with the courtesy due a teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 與周文帝結為兄弟，情寄特隆。

translations.literal: He formed brotherhood with the future Zhou founder; affection placed exceptionally high.
translations.idiomatic: He swore brotherhood with the future Zhou founder, and their bond was especially deep.

sentences.zh: 後天光敗于韓陵，節閔遂不得入關，為齊神武幽廢。

translations.literal: Later Tianguang was defeated at Hanling; Jiemin could not enter Guanzhong and was deposed and imprisoned by Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tianguang was defeated at Hanling; Jiemin never regained Guanzhong and was deposed and imprisoned by Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝即位後，神武方得志，征賀拔岳為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Shenwu could at last act on his ambitions and summoned Helü Yue as Governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, Gao Huan was free to pursue his aims and summoned Helü Yue to serve as Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 岳懼，欲單馬入朝。

translations.literal: Yue was afraid and wished to enter court alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was afraid and wanted to go to court alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 孝通乃謂嶽曰：「高王以數千鮮卑破爾硃百萬之眾，其鋒誠亦難敵。

translations.literal: Xiaotong then said to Yue: "The High King with several thousand Xianbei broke Erzhu's million-man host—their edge truly is hard to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong then told Yue, "The High King shattered Erzhu's million-man army with a few thousand Xianbei horsemen—his momentum is indeed hard to face.

sentences.zh: 然公兩兄太師、領軍，宿在其上。

translations.literal: Yet your two elder brothers the Grand Preceptor and the Commander-in-Chief long stood above him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your two elder brothers, the Grand Preceptor and the Commander-in-Chief, long outranked him.

sentences.zh: 侯深、樊子鵠、賈知、斛斯椿、大野胡也杖、吒呂延慶之徒，於爾硃之世，皆其夷等。

translations.literal: Hou Shen, Fan Zihong, Jia Zhi, Husu Chun, Daye Huyazhang, Tolü Yanqing, and the like—in the Erzhu age were all his equals in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Shen, Fan Zihong, Jia Zhi, Husu Chun, Daye Huyazhang, Tolü Yanqing, and others were all his peers in the Erzhu era.

sentences.zh: 韓陵之役，此輩前後降附，皆由事勢危逼，非其本心。

translations.literal: At Hanling these men successively surrendered—all from circumstance pressing danger, not their true hearts.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanling they surrendered one after another only because they were cornered, not from true loyalty.

sentences.zh: 在於高王，曹操之孔融，馬懿之葛誕。

translations.literal: Toward the High King they are to him as Kong Rong to Cao Cao, as Ge Dan to Sima Yi.
translations.idiomatic: To the High King they are like Kong Rong to Cao Cao, or Ge Dan to Sima Yi—men who will not submit in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 今或在京師，或據州鎮，除之又失人望，留之腹心之疾。

translations.literal: Now some are in the capital, some hold provinces—remove them and you lose popular expectation; keep them and they are disease in the bosom.
translations.idiomatic: Some are in the capital, some hold provinces; remove them and you lose men's esteem, keep them and they remain a sickness at your heart.

sentences.zh: 雖令孫騰在闕下，婁昭處鉤陳，必不能如建安之時，明矣。

translations.literal: Though Sun Teng is kept below the gate-towers and Lou Zhao at the Hooked Array, they surely cannot be as at the Jian'an era—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Sun Teng stands below the palace gates and Lou Zhao holds the inner guard, they clearly cannot bind these men as Cao Cao did at Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 以今觀之，隙難未已。

translations.literal: Viewing the present, rifts and troubles have not ended.
translations.idiomatic: As things stand now, rifts and strife are far from over.

sentences.zh: 吐萬仁雖復退逸，猶在并州，高王之計，先須平殄。

translations.literal: Tuwan Ren though withdrawn still remains in Bingzhou; the High King's plan must first pacify and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuwan Ren has withdrawn but still holds Bingzhou; the High King's first task is to crush him.

sentences.zh: 今方綏撫群雄，安置內外，何能去其巢穴，與公事關中地也？

translations.literal: Now he is soothing the many lords and settling inside and out—how could he leave his nest to contest with you, sir, for Guanzhong?
translations.idiomatic: He is busy pacifying rival powers and settling affairs at home and abroad—how could he leave his base to fight you for Guanzhong?

sentences.zh: 且六郡良家之子，三輔禮義之人，逾幽、并之驍騎，勝汝、潁之奇士，皆系仰於公，效其智力。

translations.literal: Moreover sons of good families of the six commanderies, men of ritual and righteousness of the three assists—surpassing You and Bing's fierce horsemen, excelling Ru and Ying's extraordinary men—all look up to you, sir, to devote their wit and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the sons of good families from the six commanderies and the men of ritual learning from the three metropolitan districts—horsemen fiercer than those of You and Bing, talents keener than those of Ru and Ying—all look to you to give their minds and strength.

sentences.zh: 據華山以為城雉，因黃河而為池塹；

translations.literal: Hold Mount Hua as crenellated walls, take the Yellow River as moat and ditch;
translations.idiomatic: Take Mount Hua for your battlements and the Yellow River for your moat;

sentences.zh: 退守不失封泥，進兵同于建水。

translations.literal: In retreat you lose not the sealed clay; in advance your soldiers are like those of Jianshui.
translations.idiomatic: retreat and you will not lose the passes; advance and your armies will match the hosts of old.

sentences.zh: 乃欲束手受制於人，不亦鄙乎？

translations.literal: Now you wish to bind your hands and be controlled by others—is that not base?
translations.idiomatic: Will you now fold your hands and let another master you? Is that not contemptible?

sentences.zh: 」言未卒，嶽執孝通手曰：「君言是也。

translations.literal: " Before the words were finished, Yue seized Xiaotong's hand and said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished speaking, Yue took Xiaotong by the hand and said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 」乃遜辭為啟，而不就征。

translations.literal: " He then drafted a humble memorial in reply and did not accept the summons.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wrote a deferential memorial in refusal and did not obey the summons.

sentences.zh: 太昌元年，孝通因使入朝，仍被留京師，重除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang, Xiaotong entered court on a mission and was detained in the capital; he was again appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichang, Xiaotong came to court on embassy business and was kept in the capital, where he was reappointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年三月，出為常山太守，仍以經節閔任遇故也。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Yongxi, he went out as Administrator of Changshan, still because of his former favor under Emperor Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Yongxi he was sent out as Administrator of Changshan, a post he still held on account of his earlier service and favor under Emperor Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，或稱孝通與周文友密，及樹置賀拔嶽鎮關中之計，遂見拘執，將赴晉陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, some said Xiaotong was intimate with Zhou Wen as a friend and had devised the plan to station Heba Yue to guard Guanzhong; he was then seized and was to be taken to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, reports spread that Xiaotong was on close terms with Zhou Wen and had helped devise the plan to post Heba Yue in Guanzhong; he was arrested and ordered sent to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及引見，咸為之憂。

translations.literal: When he was brought in for audience, all were anxious for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was led in to audience, everyone feared for his life.

sentences.zh: 孝通神氣從容，辭理切正，齊神武更相欽歎，即日原免。

translations.literal: Xiaotong's bearing was calm, his reasoning sharp and correct; Qi Shenwu came to admire him all the more and that same day pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong remained composed in manner and precise in argument; Gao Huan admired him all the more and pardoned him that very day.

sentences.zh: 然猶致疑忌，不加位秩，但引為坐客，時訪文典大事而已。

translations.literal: Yet suspicion still attached to him; he was given no rank or office, only kept as a seated guest and consulted from time to time on canonical texts and great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was still regarded with suspicion, however, and received no formal rank; he was kept merely as a house guest and consulted now and then on classical learning and weighty matters.

sentences.zh: 齊神武讓劍履上殿表，猶使為文。

translations.literal: For Qi Shenwu's memorial declining the privilege of wearing sword and shoes in the hall, he was still made to compose the text.
translations.idiomatic: Even the memorial in which Gao Huan declined the privilege of entering court armed and shod was drafted at his hand.

sentences.zh: 曾與諸人同詣晉祠，皆屈膝盡禮。

translations.literal: He once went with others to the Jin shrine; all knelt in full observance.
translations.idiomatic: Once, visiting the Jin shrine with a party of men, everyone else knelt and performed the full rites.

sentences.zh: 孝通獨捧手不拜，顧而言曰：「此乃諸侯之國，去吾何遠，恭而非禮，將為神笑。

translations.literal: Xiaotong alone cupped his hands and did not bow, turning to say: "This is the state of a feudal lord—how far is it from us? Reverence without proper rite will make the spirits laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong alone stood with cupped hands and did not bow, saying over his shoulder, "This is the domain of a feudal lord, not far removed from our own; reverence without proper rite will only make the spirits laugh.

sentences.zh: 」拜者漸焉。

translations.literal: " Those who had been bowing gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " One by one the bowers desisted.

sentences.zh: 興和二年，卒於鄴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xinghe he died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xinghe he died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏前二年，周文帝追軫舊好，奏贈車騎將軍、儀同三司、青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year before Wei, Zhou Wendi, recalling their old friendship, memorialized posthumous gifts of General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Two years before the Wei dynasty fell, Zhou Wendi, mindful of their old friendship, had him posthumously honored as General of Chariots and Cavalry, with rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊神武武平初，又贈鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping under Qi Shenwu, he was further granted Governor of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Wuping era in Qi, he was further posthumously named Governor of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 文集八十卷，行于時。

translations.literal: His collected writings ran to eighty juan and circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, eighty juan in all, circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 子道衡，字玄卿。

translations.literal: His son Daoheng, styled Xuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoheng, courtesy name Xuanqing.

sentences.zh: 六歲而孤，專精好學。

translations.literal: Orphaned at six, he devoted himself single-mindedly to study.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at six, he devoted himself wholly to learning.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，講《左傳》，見子產相鄭之功，作《國僑贊》，頗有詞致，見者奇之。

translations.literal: At ten he lectured on the Zuo Commentary; seeing Zichan's achievement as prime minister of Zheng, he wrote "In Praise of Guo Qiao," which had considerable literary grace, and those who saw it marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he was already expounding the Zuo Commentary; reading of Zichan's statesmanship in Zheng, he wrote "In Praise of the State-father of Guo," a piece of real literary finish that astonished all who saw it.

sentences.zh: 其後才名益著。

translations.literal: Afterward his literary fame grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter his reputation as a man of letters steadily rose.

sentences.zh: 齊司州牧、彭城王浟引為兵曹從事。

translations.literal: The Qi Governor of Sizhou, Prince of Pengcheng You, brought him in as an aide in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: You, Prince of Pengcheng and Governor of Sizhou in Qi, took him on as staff in the military bureau.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射楊愔見而嗟賞，授奉朝請。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin saw him and sighed in admiration, appointing him Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, saw him and exclaimed in admiration, granting him the title Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書隴西辛術與語，歎曰：「鄭公業不亡矣！

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Longxi Xin Shu, spoke with him and sighed: "Master Zheng's calling is not dead!
translations.idiomatic: Xin Shu of Longxi, Minister of Personnel, spoke with him and said with a sigh, "Zheng Xuan's tradition is not dead after all!

sentences.zh: 」河東裴讞目之曰：「鼎遷河朔，吾謂'關西孔子'，罕遇其人，今復遇薛君矣！」

translations.literal: " Pei Yan of Hedong fixed his gaze on him and said: "When the tripod moved to the north of the river, I said there was a 'Confucius west of the Pass' and rarely met such a man—now I meet Master Xue again!"
translations.idiomatic: " Pei Yan of Hedong looked him over and declared, "When the royal tripod shifted to the north, men spoke of a 'Confucius west of the Pass' and said such a figure was seldom found—now I have found Master Xue!"

sentences.zh: 武成即位，兼散騎常侍，接對周、陳二使。

translations.literal: When Wucheng took the throne, he was concurrently Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and received envoys from Zhou and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wucheng ascended the throne, Daoheng served concurrently as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and received the embassies of Zhou and Chen.

sentences.zh: 武平初，詔與諸儒修定五禮，除尚書左外兵郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping, by edict he joined the Confucians in revising the Five Rites and was appointed Left Outer Military Secretary in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Wuping he was ordered to join the scholars in revising the Five Rites, and was appointed Left Outer Military Secretary in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 陳使傅縡聘齊，以道衡兼主客郎接對之。

translations.literal: Chen's envoy Fu Zuan came on mission to Qi; Daoheng was made concurrent Master of Guests to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Zuan of Chen came on embassy to Qi, Daoheng was appointed concurrent Master of Guests to receive him.

sentences.zh: 縡贈詩五十韻，道衡和之，南北稱美。

translations.literal: Zuan presented a poem of fifty rhymes; Daoheng matched it, and north and south alike praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan offered a fifty-rhyme poem; Daoheng replied in kind, and both north and south rang with praise.

sentences.zh: 魏收曰：「傅縡所謂以蚓投魚耳。

translations.literal: Wei Shou said: "What Fu Zuan did was what they call throwing an earthworm to a fish.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou remarked, "Fu Zuan was only throwing earthworms to the fish."

sentences.zh: 」待詔文林館，與范陽盧思道、安平李德林齊名友善。

translations.literal: " He awaited edicts at the Wenslin Hall, famed and friendly with Lu Sidao of Fanyang and Li Delin of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: " He served as a scholar awaiting imperial orders at the Forest of Letters, and stood in equal fame and friendship with Lu Sidao of Fanyang and Li Delin of Anping.

sentences.zh: 復以本官直中書省，尋拜中書侍郎，仍參太子侍讀。

translations.literal: Again with his former office he served directly in the Secretariat; soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and still joined the Crown Prince's lecturing staff.
translations.idiomatic: He continued in his former post on duty in the Secretariat, was soon made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and also served among the Crown Prince's readers.

sentences.zh: 齊後主之世，漸見親用，與侍中斛律孝卿參預政事。

translations.literal: In the reign of the Last Lord of Qi he was gradually drawn into favor and, with Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaqing, took part in government.
translations.idiomatic: Under the last ruler of Qi he came gradually into favor and, together with Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaqing, took part in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 道衡具陳備周之策，孝卿不能用。

translations.literal: Daoheng set forth in detail a plan to guard against Zhou; Xiaqing could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng laid out in full a strategy for meeting the threat from Zhou, but Xiaqing would not act on it.

sentences.zh: 及齊亡，周武帝引為御史二命士。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Zhou Wudi brought him in as a second-grade gentleman of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi, Emperor Wu of Zhou took him on as a second-grade gentleman of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，自州主簿入為司祿上士，隋文作相，從元帥梁睿擊王謙，攝陵州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he returned home; from prefectural chief clerk he entered office as Senior Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue. When Sui Wen served as Chancellor, he followed the commander Liang Rui in attacking Wang Qian and acted as Governor of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to his native place, rose from prefectural chief clerk to Senior Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue, and when Yang Jian became Chancellor followed the commander Liang Rui against Wang Qian, serving in the interim as Governor of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大定中，授儀同，守邛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Dading era he was granted the title Yitong and held office as Governor of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading era he was granted the rank Yitong and served as Governor of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，坐事除名。

translations.literal: When Wendi received the abdication, he was struck from the rolls for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he was struck from the rolls on a charge of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 河間王弘北征突厥，召典軍書。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Hong campaigned north against the Turks and summoned him to oversee military documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hong of Hejian marched north against the Turks, he was called in to manage military correspondence.

sentences.zh: 還，除內史舍人。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Secretary of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Secretary of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其年，兼散騎常侍，聘陳使主。

translations.literal: That year he was concurrently Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and chief envoy on the embassy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he served concurrently as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and headed the embassy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 道衡因奏曰：「陛下比靈斯三代，平一九州，豈容區區之陳，久在天網之外？

translations.literal: Daoheng thereupon memorialized: "Your Majesty's virtue equals the Three Dynasties and has pacified the Nine Provinces—how can petty Chen long remain outside the imperial net?
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng memorialized, "Your Majesty's virtue matches the Three Dynasties and you have brought the Nine Provinces to peace—how can a petty Chen remain long outside the imperial net?

sentences.zh: 臣今奉使，請責以稱蕃。

translations.literal: Your servant now goes on mission and asks leave to demand that they declare themselves a tributary state.
translations.idiomatic: On this mission I ask leave to demand that they acknowledge themselves a tributary state.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕且含養，致之度外，勿以言辭相折。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "For now I shall cherish and nurture them, set them beyond measure, and not break them with harsh words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "For now I shall cherish and forbear with them, set them beyond ordinary reckoning, and not break them with sharp words."

sentences.zh: 」江東雅好篇什，陳主尤愛雕蟲，道衡每有所作，南人無不吟誦焉。

translations.literal: " East of the river they have long loved verse; the Lord of Chen especially delights in ornamental writing—whenever Daoheng produced a piece, the southerners all chanted and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: " The southeast has always loved poetry; the Chen ruler above all dotes on ornamental verse—and whenever Daoheng wrote something new, the southerners chanted it throughout their lands.

sentences.zh: 及八年伐陳，拜淮南道行台尚書吏部郎，兼掌文翰。

translations.literal: When in the eighth year Chen was attacked, he was appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel of the Huainan Circuit Mobile Secretariat and also oversaw documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the campaign against Chen began, he was appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel on the Huainan circuit secretariat and also directed literary affairs.

sentences.zh: 王師臨江，高熲夜幕中，謂曰：「今段定克江東以不？

translations.literal: As the imperial army reached the Yangtze, Gao Jiong in the darkness of night said to him: "This time, will we surely take the lands east of the river?
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial armies reached the Yangtze, Gao Jiong said to him one night within the tent: "Will we take the southeast this time or not?

sentences.zh: 君試言之。

translations.literal: Try telling me.
translations.idiomatic: Tell me what you think."

sentences.zh: 」道衡答曰：「凡論大事成敗，先須以至理斷之。

translations.literal: " Daoheng answered: "Whenever one discusses the success or failure of great affairs, one must first judge them by supreme principle.
translations.idiomatic: " Daoheng answered, "Whenever one weighs the outcome of a great affair, one must first judge it by the highest principle.

sentences.zh: 《禹貢》所載九州，本是王者封域。

translations.literal: The Nine Provinces recorded in the Tribute of Yu were originally the demesne of the king.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Provinces recorded in the Tribute of Yu were originally the domain of the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 郭璞有云：'江東偏王三百年，還與中國合。

translations.literal: Guo Pu said: 'The partial kings east of the river for three hundred years will return and unite with the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu said, 'The petty kings east of the river hold sway for three hundred years, then return to union with the Central States.'

sentences.zh: '今數將滿矣。

translations.literal: ' That term is now nearly complete.
translations.idiomatic: ' That term is nearly spent.

sentences.zh: 以運數而言，其必克一也。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of fate and number, the first certainty of victory is this.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by the turn of fate and number, the first certainty of victory lies here.

sentences.zh: 有德者昌，無德者亡，自古興滅，皆由此道。

translations.literal: Those with virtue flourish; those without perish—from antiquity rise and fall have all followed this way.
translations.idiomatic: Those with virtue flourish and those without perish; rise and fall have followed this law since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 主上躬履恭儉，憂勞庶政。

translations.literal: Our lord personally practices reverence and frugality and toils over the myriad affairs of government.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign himself practices reverence and frugality and labors over the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 叔寶峻宇雕牆，酣酒荒色。

translations.literal: Shubao raises lofty halls and carved walls, drowning in wine and lost to lust.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao raises towering halls and carved walls, drowning in wine and lost to pleasure.

sentences.zh: 其必克二也。

translations.literal: The second certainty of victory is this.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second certainty of victory.

sentences.zh: 為國之體，在於任寄。

translations.literal: The substance of governing a state lies in whom one entrusts with office.
translations.idiomatic: The substance of governing a state lies in whom one entrusts with power.

sentences.zh: 彼之公卿，備員而已。

translations.literal: Their high ministers are mere placeholders.
translations.idiomatic: Their ministers and grandees are mere placeholders.

sentences.zh: 拔小人施文慶，委以政事；

translations.literal: They elevated the petty man Shi Wenqing and entrusted him with government;
translations.idiomatic: They elevated the petty man Shi Wenqing and entrusted him with government;

sentences.zh: 尚書令江總唯事詩酒，本非經略之才；

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Jiang Zong attends only to verse and wine—no talent for strategy by nature;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Jiang Zong cares only for wine and poetry and was never a man for strategy;

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶、任蠻奴是其大將，一夫之用耳。

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe and Ren Mannu are their great generals—fit for a single man's use alone.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe and Ren Mannu are their chief generals—men useful in a brawl, not in a war.

sentences.zh: 其必克三也。

translations.literal: This is surely the third reason for victory.
translations.idiomatic: The third certainty of victory is here.

sentences.zh: 我有道而大，彼無德而小。

translations.literal: We have the Way and are great; they lack virtue and are small.
translations.idiomatic: We possess the Way and stand large; they lack virtue and are small.

sentences.zh: 量其甲士，不過十萬，西自巫峽，東極滄海，分之則勢懸而力弱；

translations.literal: Counting their armed men, they do not exceed a hundred thousand—from Witch Gorge west to the eastern sea; divided their force hangs in air and strength grows weak;
translations.idiomatic: Count their soldiers and they are no more than a hundred thousand; from Witch Gorge to the eastern sea, split they are overmatched and weak,

sentences.zh: 聚之則守此而失彼。

translations.literal: gathered they hold here and lose there.
translations.idiomatic: gathered they must defend one place and abandon another.

sentences.zh: 其必克四也。

translations.literal: This is surely the fourth reason for victory.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth certainty of victory is here.

sentences.zh: 席捲之勢，其在不疑。

translations.literal: A sweeping tide—its coming admits no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The tide that sweeps all before it leaves no room for doubt.

sentences.zh: 」熲忻然曰：「君言成敗，理甚分明。

translations.literal: " Jiong said gladly: "Your words on success and failure are very clear in reason.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiong said with satisfaction, "Your reasoning on victory and defeat could not be clearer.

sentences.zh: 本以才學相期，不意籌略乃爾。

translations.literal: I originally expected talent in letters—I did not think strategy would be thus.
translations.idiomatic: I counted on you for letters; I did not know your counsel ran so deep.

sentences.zh: 」還除吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: " On return he was made Vice Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: " On his return he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 後坐抽擢人物，有言其党蘇威，任人有意故，除名，配防嶺表。

translations.literal: Later for promoting men he was charged with faction for Su Wei, appointing with partial intent—struck from the rolls, sent to guard the southern marches.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was accused of promoting men and of building a faction around Su Wei and favoring appointees for private reasons; he was struck from the rolls and sent to guard the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣時在揚州，陰令人諷道衡，遣從揚州路，將奏留之。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang was then in Yangzhou and secretly sent men to hint Daoheng should take the Yangzhou road—he would memorialize to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guang of Jin was then at Yangzhou and secretly sent word urging Daoheng to travel by way of Yangzhou so he could memorialize the throne to keep him there.

sentences.zh: 道衡不樂王府，用漢王諒之計，遂出江陵道而貙Ｑ擺詉骰梗髗蹦謔肥＝绡跤墒竅沃湏Ｈ話磘洳牛饀唐募滗瘛：笫镡輳罎諛謔肥湯桑拎由弦峭礆镡盡５籃餉抗刮模㗾匾毁饂照礴１詼髢裕蘯嘔粧庥腥吮閂嘑杧瀋蛩既緔恕５勖吭唬骸暗籃庾魑氖槌莆乙狻！

translations.literal: Daoheng disliked a prince's household; using Prince of Han Liang's plan he took the Jiangling road and left.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng had no wish to serve in a princely house; at Prince Liang of Han's suggestion he left by the road through Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 比喚脛竝雜氐湏：蟮畚窖釧亍⑴：朐唬旱籃飫弦櫻浲镨骨誒停飈聳鉤p門陳戟。

translations.literal: Soon an edict recalled him to serve directly in the Secretariat. The Prince of Jin resented this but loved his talent and still treated him with some courtesy. Later Gaozu was pleased with his diligence and said to Yang Su and Niu Hong, "Daoheng is old; we drive him with labor—he ought to have vermilion gates and halberds before his door.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict recalled him, and he served in the Secretariat directly. Prince Guang bore a grudge for it, yet prized his talent and still showed him courtesy. Later Emperor Wen was pleased with his service and said to Yang Su and Niu Hong, "Daoheng is aged and worn with our demands; he ought to have vermilion gates and halberds posted at his door.

sentences.zh: 」於是進上開府，賜物百段。

translations.literal: " He was then advanced to Upper Palace Attendant and given a hundred bales of goods.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then promoted to Upper Palace Attendant, First Rank, and given a hundred bales of gifts.

sentences.zh: 道衡辭以無功。

translations.literal: Daoheng declined on the ground of no merit.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng declined, saying he had earned no such reward.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾久勞階陛，國家大事，皆爾宣行，豈非爾功也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You have long toiled on the court steps; great affairs of state—all have passed through your proclamation—is that not your merit?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have long labored on the steps of my hall; the great affairs of state have all passed through your hand—is that not merit enough?"

sentences.zh: 道衡久當樞要，才名益顯。

translations.literal: Daoheng long held the pivot, his literary fame ever brighter.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng had long stood at the heart of power, and his fame for talent only grew.

sentences.zh: 太子、諸王爭與交好，高熲、楊素雅相推重，聲名籍甚，無競一時。

translations.literal: Heir and princes vied to befriend him; Gao Jiong and Yang Su deeply esteemed him—fame filled the registers, unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and imperial princes vied for his friendship; Gao Jiong and Yang Su held him in the highest regard; his name filled every register and had no rival in the day.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，楊素專掌朝政。

translations.literal: In Renshou Yang Su alone held court government.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign Yang Su held court power in his hands alone.

sentences.zh: 道衡既與素善，上不欲道衡久知機密，因出檢校襄州總管。

translations.literal: Daoheng being friendly with Su, the emperor did not wish him long to know secrets—so sent him out to inspect the Xiangzhou commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng was close to Su, and the emperor did not want him near secrets too long; he sent him out as overseer of the Xiangzhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 道衡一旦見出，不勝悲戀，言之哽咽。

translations.literal: Daoheng at once seeing himself out, could not bear grief and longing—speaking he choked.
translations.idiomatic: Torn from court in a day, Daoheng could not master his grief; his voice broke when he spoke.

sentences.zh: 帝愴然改容曰：「爾光陰晚暮，侍奉誠勞，朕欲令爾將攝。

translations.literal: The emperor sadly changed countenance and said: "Your years are late dusk; your service has been truly weary—I wished to have you take the reins.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face softened with sorrow and he said, "Your years are in their dusk, and your service has been loyal and hard; I wished you to take charge of affairs for me.

sentences.zh: 今爾之去，朕如斷一臂。

translations.literal: Now with your going I am as if one arm were cut."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you leave, it is as if I were losing an arm."

sentences.zh: 」於是賚物三百段，九環金帶並時服一襲，馬十匹，慰勉遣之。

translations.literal: " He then granted three hundred bales of goods, a nine-ring gold belt with one suit of seasonal dress, ten horses, comforted and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: " He bestowed three hundred bales of goods, a nine-ring gold belt, a set of court dress, and ten horses, and sent him off with words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 在任清簡，吏人懷其惠。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and simple; clerks and people cherished his grace.
translations.idiomatic: In office he ruled with clarity and restraint, and clerks and common people alike cherished his kindness.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，轉潘州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang succeeded and he was transferred to Governor of Panzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was made Governor of Panzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，上表求致仕。

translations.literal: After a year and more he memorialized requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he memorialized asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝謂內史侍郎虞世基曰：「道衡將至，當以秘書監待之。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Secretariat Vice-Director Yu Shiji: "When Daoheng arrives he should be treated as Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yu Shiji, Vice Director of the Secretariat, "When Daoheng comes I mean to receive him as Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 」道衡既至，上《高祖文皇帝頌》。

translations.literal: " When Daoheng arrived he presented "Eulogy to Emperor Gaozu."
translations.idiomatic: " When Daoheng arrived he presented his "Eulogy to Emperor Wen."

sentences.zh: 帝覽之不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor reading it was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 顧謂蘇威曰：「道衡致美先朝，此魚藻之義也。

translations.literal: Turning he said to Su Wei: "Daoheng heaps beauty on the former reign—this has the sense of 'Fish and Water-weeds.'"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Su Wei and said, "Daoheng lavishes praise on the former reign—that is the meaning of 'Fish and Water-weeds.'"

sentences.zh: 」於是拜司隸大夫，將置之罪。

translations.literal: " He was then made Minister of the Metropolitan Inspectorate, about to set a crime upon him.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Metropolitan Minister of the Inspecting Office, and the emperor meant to bring him to ruin.

sentences.zh: 道衡不悟，司隸刺史房彥謙素與相善，知必及禍，勸之杜絕賓客，卑辭下氣，而道衡不能用。

translations.literal: Daoheng did not perceive; Metropolitan Censor Fang Yanqian had long been his friend, knew disaster must come, urged him to cut off guests, humble speech and lower breath—Daoheng could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng did not understand; Fang Yanqian, Metropolitan Inspector, who had long been his friend, knew ruin was certain and urged him to refuse visitors and speak with humble deference, but Daoheng would not listen.

sentences.zh: 會議新令，久不能決，道衡謂朝士曰：「向使高熲不死，令當久行。

translations.literal: Meeting to discuss new statutes, long unable to decide, Daoheng told court gentlemen: "Had Gao Jiong not died, these statutes would long have been in force.
translations.idiomatic: At a meeting on the new statutes, when deliberation dragged on, Daoheng told the court gentlemen, "If Gao Jiong still lived, these laws would long since have been in force.

sentences.zh: 」有人奏之。

translations.literal: " Someone memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: " Someone reported his words to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「汝憶熲乎？

translations.literal: The emperor raged: "Do you miss Jiong?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flared with anger and said, "Do you mourn Jiong?"

sentences.zh: 」付執法者推之。

translations.literal: " He was handed to law officers for prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: " He was handed to the law officers to be tried.

sentences.zh: 道衡自以非大過，促憲司早解。

translations.literal: Daoheng himself thinking it no great offense, urged the censorate to release him soon.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng judged the offense slight and pressed the censorate to release him quickly.

sentences.zh: 奏日，冀帝赦之，敕家人具饌以備客來侯者。

translations.literal: On the day of the memorial, he hoped the Emperor would pardon him, and ordered the household to prepare provisions against guests coming to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the day his petition was submitted, he still hoped for imperial mercy and told his household to lay out a feast for the guests who would surely come to congratulate him.

sentences.zh: 及奏，帝令自盡。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the Emperor ordered him to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: When it was read, the Emperor commanded him to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 道衡殊不意，未能引訣。

translations.literal: Daoheng had not expected this at all and could not bring himself to the noose.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng was utterly unprepared and could not bring himself to accept the sentence.

sentences.zh: 憲司重奏，縊而殺之。

translations.literal: The imperial censorate submitted again, and he was strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate memorialized again, and he was strangled.

sentences.zh: 妻子徙且末。

translations.literal: His wife and children were exiled to Qimo.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children were banished to Qimo.

sentences.zh: 時年七十。

translations.literal: At the time he was seventy years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy years old.

sentences.zh: 天下冤之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: The empire held his death a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 有集七十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in seventy scrolls, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A seventy-scroll collection of his writings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 有子五人，收最知名，出後族父孺。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Shou was the most renowned, and was made heir to his clansman father's son Ru.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons. Shou was the best known; he was given in adoption to his cousin Ru.

sentences.zh: 孺清貞孤介，不交流俗。

translations.literal: Ru was pure, upright, aloof and solitary, and did not associate with the vulgar crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Ru was chaste, solitary, and proud, never mixing with common society.

sentences.zh: 涉歷經史，有才思，雖不為大文，所有詩詠，大致清遠。

translations.literal: He ranged through the classics and histories, had literary talent; though he did not write great prose, his poems were in general pure and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the classics and histories and gifted with wit; though he never composed grand essays, his poems tended toward clarity and distance.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為侍御史、揚州總管司功參軍。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he served as Attending Censor and Registrar of the Yangzhou Regional Commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaihuang he served as Attending Censor and Registrar under the Yangzhou commandery headquarters.

sentences.zh: 每以方直自處，府寮多不便之。

translations.literal: He always conducted himself by square uprightness, and many colleagues in the office found it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: He always held himself to uncompromising rectitude, which made many of his colleagues uneasy.

sentences.zh: 卒於襄城郡掾。

translations.literal: He died in the post of Registrar of Xiangcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as commandery registrar of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 所蒞官皆有能名。

translations.literal: Every office he held won him a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held he was known for competence.

sentences.zh: 道衡偏相友愛，收初生，即與孺為後。

translations.literal: Daoheng was especially close and affectionate toward him; when Shou was newly born he at once gave him to Ru as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng cherished him above the rest; when Shou was born, he was immediately given to Ru as his heir.

sentences.zh: 養于孺宅，至於成長，殆不識本生。

translations.literal: Nurtured in Ru's household, by the time he grew up he scarcely knew his birth parents.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in Ru's house, he grew to adulthood hardly knowing his birth parents.

sentences.zh: 太常丞胡仲操曾在朝堂就孺借刀子割爪甲。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonies Assistant Hu Zhongcao once in court asked Ru to borrow a knife to trim his fingernails.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhongcao, an assistant in the Directorate of Ceremonies, once asked Ru on the palace floor to lend him a knife to pare his nails.

sentences.zh: 孺以仲操非雅士，竟不與之。

translations.literal: Ru, considering Zhongcao no cultivated gentleman, ultimately would not give it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ru judged Zhongcao no man of refinement and refused him outright.

sentences.zh: 其不肯妄交，清介獨行，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His refusal to make rash acquaintances and his pure integrity walking alone were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His refusal of casual acquaintance and his austere independence were characteristic in this way.

sentences.zh: 道衡兄溫，字尼卿。

translations.literal: Daoheng's elder brother Wen, styled Niqing.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng's elder brother Wen, courtesy name Niqing.

sentences.zh: 沈敏有器局，博覽墳典，尤善隸書。

translations.literal: Deeply perceptive with capacity and compass, he broadly perused the ancients' texts, especially skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and keen, possessed of breadth of vision, he studied the ancient canon extensively and excelled especially at clerical script calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 仕周為上黃郡守。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as Administrator of Shanghuang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he was Administrator of Shanghuang.

sentences.zh: 周平齊，徙燕郡太守，以簡惠稱。

translations.literal: When Zhou pacified Qi he was transferred to Grand Administrator of Yan commandery, renowned for simplicity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou conquered Qi he was moved to Grand Administrator of Yan, famed for simple benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，賜爵齊安縣子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was granted the noble rank of Viscount of Qi'an county.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he received the title Viscount of Qi'an.

sentences.zh: 卒於郡。

translations.literal: He died in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子邁嗣。

translations.literal: His son Mai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mai inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 邁字弘仁，性寡言，長於詞辯。

translations.literal: Mai styled Hongren, by nature sparing of speech, skilled in rhetorical disputation.
translations.idiomatic: Mai, courtesy name Hongren, was taciturn by nature but fluent in debate.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，襲爵齊安子，改封鐘山。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he inherited the rank of Viscount of Qi'an, then was re-enfeoffed at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he inherited the Qi'an viscounty and was later enfeoffed at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 歷位太子舍人。

translations.literal: He successively held the post of Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an attendant in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為刑部、選部二侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was Vice Director of both the Punishments and Selection Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye he was Vice Director of Punishments and of Selection.

sentences.zh: 道衡從父弟道實，位禮部侍郎、離石郡太守，知名于世。

translations.literal: Daoheng's younger cousin by the father's line Daoshi, held the posts of Vice Director of Rites and Grand Administrator of Lishi commandery, renowned in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng's paternal cousin Daoshi rose to Vice Director of Rites and Grand Administrator of Lishi and was known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 從子德音，有俊才，起家游騎尉。

translations.literal: His nephew Deyin had outstanding talent and began his career as Commandant of Roaming Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Deyin, a man of bright gifts, entered service as Commandant of Roaming Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 佐魏淡修《魏史》，史成，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He assisted Wei Dan in compiling the History of Wei; when the history was completed he was promoted to Assistant in the Bureau of Authorship.
translations.idiomatic: He helped Wei Dan compile the History of Wei and, when it was finished, was promoted to assistant compiler in the Bureau of Authorship.

sentences.zh: 及越王侗稱制東都，王世充之僭號，軍書羽檄，皆出其手。

translations.literal: When Prince Kuai of Yue held power in the Eastern Capital and Wang Shichong usurped the throne, military documents and urgent proclamations all came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kuai of Yue ruled at the eastern capital and Wang Shichong seized the throne, every dispatch and call to arms bore his hand.

sentences.zh: 世充平，以罪誅。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified, he was executed for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichong's defeat he was executed for complicity.

sentences.zh: 其文筆多行於世。

translations.literal: His writings circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Much of his writing still circulated.

sentences.zh: 聰弟和，南青州刺史。

translations.literal: Cong's younger brother He, Governor of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's younger brother He served as Governor of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 和子善。

translations.literal: He's son Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He's son was Shan.

sentences.zh: 善字仲良。

translations.literal: Shan styled Zhongliang.
translations.idiomatic: Shan, courtesy name Zhongliang.

sentences.zh: 少為司空府參軍。

translations.literal: In youth he was a staff officer in the Commandant of Works office.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a junior officer in the Secretariat of Works.

sentences.zh: 再遷鹽池都將。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Commander of the Salt Ponds.
translations.idiomatic: He rose twice to command the salt-works garrison.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，魏改河東為秦州，以善為別駕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Wei renamed Hedong as Qinzhou and appointed Shan Vice Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, the Wei renamed Hedong as Qinzhou and made Shan its vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 善家素富，僮僕數百人。

translations.literal: Shan's family had long been wealthy, with several hundred servant boys.
translations.idiomatic: The Shan household was old wealth, with hundreds in their retinue.

sentences.zh: 兄元信，杖氣豪侈，每食方丈，坐客恆滿，弦歌不絕；

translations.literal: His elder brother Yuanxin relied on spirit and lived lavishly; every meal filled a square zhang, guests were always full, string and song unceasing;
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yuanxin swaggered and spent freely—his table could fill a hall, his guests never thinned, music never ceased;

sentences.zh: 而善獨恭己率素，愛樂閒靜。

translations.literal: yet Shan alone was reverent and led a plain life, loving ease and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: while Shan alone lived modestly and cherished stillness.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，齊神武敗于沙苑，留善族兄崇禮守河東。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Qi Shenwu was defeated at Shayuan and left Shan's clansman elder brother Chongli to hold Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, when Qi Shenwu was routed at Shayuan, he left Shan's kinsman Chongli to defend Hedong.

sentences.zh: 周文帝遣李弼圍之，崇禮固守不下。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Wen sent Li Bi to besiege it; Chongli held firm and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou sent Li Bi to besiege the city, but Chongli held out and would not fall.

sentences.zh: 善密說崇禮，猶持疑不決。

translations.literal: Shan secretly urged Chongli, yet he still hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Shan urged Chongli in secret, but Chongli still wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 會善從弟馥妹夫高子信為防城都督，守城南面，遣馥來詣善，云「意欲應接西軍，但恐力所不制。

translations.literal: It happened that Shan's younger cousin Fu's brother-in-law Gao Zixin was Defense Commander, holding the south of the city; he sent Fu to visit Shan, saying, "I wish to welcome the western army, but fear my strength cannot control the situation."
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shan's cousin Fu's brother-in-law Gao Zixin, defense commander on the south wall, sent Fu to Shan with word: "We mean to admit the western army, but fear we lack the strength to see it through."

sentences.zh: 」善即令弟濟將門生數十人，與信、馥等斬關引弼軍入。

translations.literal: " Shan at once ordered his younger brother Ji to lead several dozen disciples, and with Xin, Fu and others cut the pass and led Bi's army in.
translations.idiomatic: " Shan then sent his brother Ji with several dozen retainers; together with Xin, Fu, and the rest they cut the gate chains and admitted Li Bi's troops.

sentences.zh: 時預謀者並賞五等爵。

translations.literal: At the time all who had taken part in the plot were rewarded with fifth-rank nobility.
translations.idiomatic: All who had plotted with them were rewarded with fifth-rank titles.

sentences.zh: 善以背逆歸順，臣子常情，豈容闔門大小俱叨封邑，遂與弟慎並固辭不受。

translations.literal: Shan said that turning from rebellion to submission was the common feeling of subject and minister—how could the whole household, great and small, all receive fiefs? He and his younger brother Shen therefore firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shan held that deserting a doomed cause for the victor was only what any loyal subject would do—surely the whole clan could not claim fiefs for it. He and his brother Shen refused the rewards outright.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉之，以善為汾陰令。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen commended him and appointed Shan Magistrate of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised him and made him Magistrate of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 善幹用強明，一郡稱最。

translations.literal: Shan was capable and forceful in administration, and the whole commandery called him foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Shan governed with force and clarity; within the commandery none ranked above him.

sentences.zh: 太守王羆美之，令善兼督六縣事。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Wang Pi admired him and had Shan additionally supervise the affairs of six counties.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Wang Pi admired his work and put him in charge of six counties as well.

sentences.zh: 尋為行台郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he became Gentleman of the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a secretary on the mobile staff.

sentences.zh: 時欲廣置屯田以供軍費，乃除司農少卿，領同州夏陽縣二十屯監。

translations.literal: At the time they wished broadly to establish military colonies to supply army expenses, so he was appointed Vice Minister of Agriculture and oversaw twenty colony supervisors in Xiayang county, Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought to expand military colonies to fund the armies, he was made Vice Minister of Agriculture and superintendent of twenty colony offices in Xiayang, Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 又于夏陽諸山置鐵冶，復令善為監，每月役八千人，營造軍器。

translations.literal: They also established ironworks in the mountains of Xiayang and again made Shan superintendent; each month eight thousand men were conscripted to manufacture military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Ironworks were set up in the Xiayang hills and Shan was again put in charge; every month eight thousand laborers forged weapons for the army.

sentences.zh: 善自督課，兼加慰撫，甲兵精利而皆忘其苦焉。

translations.literal: Shan personally supervised the labor and also offered comfort; arms and armor were keen-edged yet all forgot their hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Shan oversaw the work himself and treated the men kindly; arms came out sharp and fine, and the workers scarcely felt their burden.

sentences.zh: 遷大丞相府從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Gentleman in the Grand Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attending gentleman in the Grand Chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 追論屯田功，賜爵龍門縣子。

translations.literal: His military-colony achievements were reviewed retrospectively and he was granted the rank of Viscount of Longmen county.
translations.idiomatic: His service in the colonies was recognized and he was ennobled Viscount of Longmen.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎，除河東郡守，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, appointed Administrator of Hedong commandery, advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Opening an Office Equal to the Three Excellencies, and granted the surname of the Yuwen clan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Hedong, was made General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and received the imperial surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜工部中大夫，進爵博平縣公。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established he was appointed Grand Master of the Ministry of Works and advanced in rank to Duke of Boping county.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were created he became Grand Master of Works and was raised to Duke of Boping.

sentences.zh: 再遷戶部中大夫。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Grand Master of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was later moved to Grand Master of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護執政，儀同齊軌語善云：「兵馬萬機，須歸天子，何因猶在權門，」善白之，護乃殺軌。

translations.literal: At the time Duke of Jin Hu held power; Palace Attendant of the First Order Qi Gui said to Shan, "Arms and the myriad affairs of state must return to the Son of Heaven—why do they still rest in the gate of power?" Shan reported this, and Hu then killed Gui.
translations.idiomatic: While Duke Hu of Jin held the reins, Qi Gui, a palace attendant of the first order, told Shan: "Arms and every weight of government belong to the Son of Heaven—why do they still sit in a minister's hands?" Shan reported the remark, and Hu had Gui executed.

sentences.zh: 以善忠於己，引為中外府司馬，遷司會中大夫，副總六府事。
