translations.literal: Because Shan was loyal to him, he drew him in as Marshal of the Inner and Outer Offices, transferred him to Grand Master of the Office of Accounts, and made him deputy overseer of the Six Offices' affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taking Shan's loyalty as proof, Hu made him marshal of the inner and outer staffs, then Grand Master of Accounts and deputy head of the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 加授京兆尹，仍行司會。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Intendant of Jingzhao while still acting as Master of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Intendant of the capital district while continuing to run the Office of Accounts.

sentences.zh: 出為隆州刺史，兼益州總管府長史。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Longzhou and concurrently Chief Clerk of the Yizhou Regional Commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Longzhou and chief clerk under the Yizhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 徵拜武威少府。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Wuwu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as vice director of the Wuwu Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈三州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given the post of Governor of the three provinces of Sanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Sanzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝以善告齊軌事，諡曰繆公。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Shan had reported Qi Gui's affair, gave him the posthumous title Duke Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shan had informed on Qi Gui, the Emperor gave him the posthumous name Duke Mu.

sentences.zh: 子褒嗣，官至高陽郡守。

translations.literal: His son Bao succeeded; in office he rose to Administrator of Gaoyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao inherited his line and rose to Administrator of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 善弟慎，字伯護。

translations.literal: Shan's younger brother Shen, styled Bohu.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's younger brother Shen, courtesy name Bohu.

sentences.zh: 好學，能屬文，善草書。

translations.literal: He loved learning, could compose prose, and was skilled in cursive script.
translations.idiomatic: He loved study, could write well, and excelled at cursive calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 與同郡裴叔逸、裴諏之、柳虯、范陽盧柔、隴西李璨並友善。

translations.literal: With his fellow commandery-men Pei Shuyi, Pei Xunzhi, Liu Qiu, Fan-yang Lu Rou, and Longxi Li Can he was all on friendly terms.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Pei Shuyi, Pei Xunzhi, Liu Qiu, Lu Rou of Fanyang, and Li Can of Longxi, all men of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 起家丞相府墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as a staff officer in the Ink Office of the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a clerk in the chancellor's ink office.

sentences.zh: 周文於行台省置學，取丞郎及府佐德行明敏者充生。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen established a school at the Mobile Secretariat and selected assistant directors and office aides of clear virtue and keen intelligence to serve as students.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen founded a school at the mobile secretariat and enrolled assistant directors and staff of proven virtue and sharp mind.

sentences.zh: 悉令旦理公務，晚就講習，先《六經》，後子史。

translations.literal: All were ordered to handle public business in the morning and attend lectures in the evening, first the Six Classics, then the masters and histories.
translations.idiomatic: They handled official work by day and studied in the evening—first the Six Classics, then the philosophers and histories.

sentences.zh: 又于諸生中簡德行淳懿者侍讀書。

translations.literal: From among the students he further selected those of pure virtue and honest bearing to attend and read books.
translations.idiomatic: From the students he chose those of the purest character to attend him in reading.

sentences.zh: 慎與李璨及隴西李伯良、辛韶、武功蘇衡、譙郡夏侯裕、安定梁曠、梁禮、河南長孫璋、河東裴舉、薛同、滎陽鄭朝等十二人，並應其選。

translations.literal: Shen and Li Can, together with Longxi Li Boliang, Xin Shao, Wugong Su Heng, Qiao commandery Xiahou Yu, Anding Liang Kuang, Liang Li, Henan Zhangsun Zhang, Hedong Pei Ju, Xue Tong, Xingyang Zheng Chao and eleven others, all met the selection.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, Li Can, and ten others—Li Boliang of Longxi, Xin Shao, Su Heng of Wugong, Xiahou Yu of Qiao, Liang Kuang and Liang Li of Anding, Zhangsun Zhang of Henan, Pei Ju of Hedong, Xue Tong, and Zheng Chao of Xingyang—were all chosen.

sentences.zh: 又以慎為學師，以知諸生課業。

translations.literal: Shen was again made school master to oversee the students' coursework.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was also made master of the school, charged with the students' progress.

sentences.zh: 周文雅好談論，並簡名僧深識玄宗者一百人，於第內講說。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen elegantly loved discourse and also selected a hundred renowned monks of deep insight into the mysterious teaching to lecture within his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen delighted in learned talk and gathered a hundred eminent monks versed in the deeper doctrines to lecture at his mansion.

sentences.zh: 又命慎等十二人兼學佛義，使內外俱通。

translations.literal: He also ordered Shen and the twelve others to study Buddhist doctrine as well, so that inner and outer learning would both be mastered.
translations.idiomatic: He also required Shen and the twelve to study Buddhist teaching, that they might be versed in both worlds of learning.

sentences.zh: 由是四方競為大乘學。

translations.literal: From this the four quarters vied in taking up Mahayana studies.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the realm turned eagerly to Mahayana study.

sentences.zh: 在學數年，復以慎為宜都公侍讀。

translations.literal: After several years in the school, Shen was again made Reader-in-Attendance to the Duke of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in the school he was made reader to the Duke of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜膳部下大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established he was appointed Grand Master of the Commissariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were created he became Grand Master of the Commissariat.

sentences.zh: 慎兄善又任工部，並居清顯，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Shen's elder brother Shan also held the Ministry of Works; both occupied pure and eminent posts, and men of the age took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's elder brother Shan held the Ministry of Works; both brothers sat in lofty offices, and their contemporaries counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，除禦正下大夫，封淮南縣子。

translations.literal: When Zhou Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Shen was appointed Lower Grand Master of the Imperial Rectifier and enfeoffed as Viscount of Huainan county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Shen was made lower grand master of the imperial rectifier and enfeoffed Viscount of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 曆師氏、禦伯中大夫。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Grand Master of the Masters' Clan and Grand Master of the Imperial Charioteer.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as grand master of the masters' clan and grand master of the imperial charioteer.

sentences.zh: 保定初，出為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he went out as Governor of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoding era he was sent out as Governor of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 界既雜蠻夷，恆以劫掠為務。

translations.literal: The borderlands were already mixed with barbarians and Yi peoples, who constantly made raiding their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction was thick with tribal peoples who lived by raiding.

sentences.zh: 慎乃集諸豪帥，具宣朝旨，仍令首領每月一參，或須言事者，不限時節。

translations.literal: Shen then gathered all the powerful chieftains, fully proclaimed the court's intent, and further ordered the leaders to attend audience once a month; those who needed to speak on affairs were not limited by season or hour.
translations.idiomatic: Shen summoned the tribal chiefs, set forth the court's will, and required the headmen to attend him monthly; any who had business to report might come at any time.

sentences.zh: 慎每見，必殷勤勸誡，及賜酒食。

translations.literal: Whenever Shen received them he was sure to urge them earnestly and admonish them, and also bestow wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: At every audience he exhorted them warmly and set out wine and food.

sentences.zh: 一年之間，翕然從化。

translations.literal: Within a single year they all at once submitted to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year they submitted to his rule as one.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻乃相謂曰：「今日始知刺史真人父母也。

translations.literal: The various barbarians then said to one another, "Only today do we know the Governor is truly our father and mother."
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen said among themselves: "Only now do we know our governor is father and mother to us in truth."

sentences.zh: 」莫不欣悅。

translations.literal: " None failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: " All were filled with joy.

sentences.zh: 自是繈負而至者千餘戶。

translations.literal: From this time more than a thousand households came carrying infants on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: After that more than a thousand households came in, children strapped to their backs.

sentences.zh: 蠻俗，婚娶之後，父母雖在，即與別居。

translations.literal: By barbarian custom, after marriage, though the parents were still alive, they at once lived apart.
translations.idiomatic: Among the tribes it was custom that after marriage, even while parents still lived, the couple set up a separate household.

sentences.zh: 慎謂守令曰：「牧守令長是化人者也，豈有其子娶妻，便與父母離析？

translations.literal: Shen told the prefects and magistrates: "Governors, prefects, magistrates, and chiefs are those who transform the people—how can it be that when sons take wives they at once separate from their parents?
translations.idiomatic: Shen told the prefectural and county officials, "Governors and magistrates exist to transform the people. How can sons marry and at once leave their parents?

sentences.zh: 非唯萌俗之失，亦是牧守之罪。

translations.literal: This is not only a failing of emerging custom but also the crime of governors and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: That is not only a failing of popular custom but also a fault of those who govern.

sentences.zh: 」慎乃親自誘導，示以孝慈。

translations.literal: " Shen thereupon personally guided them, showing them filial piety and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen thereupon guided them himself, teaching filial piety and kindness.

sentences.zh: 並遣守令，各喻所部。

translations.literal: He also sent out prefects and magistrates, each to instruct his own jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent each official to instruct his own district.

sentences.zh: 有數戶蠻，別居數年，遂還侍養，及行得果膳，歸奉父母。

translations.literal: Several barbarian households, having lived apart for years, then returned to wait upon and support their parents; when traveling and obtaining fruit or delicacies, they brought them home to offer to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: Several tribal households that had lived apart for years returned to serve their parents, and when they obtained fruit or delicacies on the road they brought them home as offerings.

sentences.zh: 慎以其從善之速，具以狀聞，有詔蠲其賦役。

translations.literal: Because of their speed in turning to goodness, Shen reported the matter in full, and an imperial decree exempted them from taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by how quickly they reformed, Shen reported the matter in full, and an edict exempted them from taxes and corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 於是風化大行，有同華俗。

translations.literal: Thereupon moral transformation spread widely, becoming the same as Chinese custom.
translations.idiomatic: Exemplary customs then spread widely until they resembled those of the Chinese.

sentences.zh: 尋為蕃部中大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Middle Grand Master of the Barbarian Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to serve as middle grand master in the Office of Barbarian Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以疾去職，卒於家。

translations.literal: Due to illness he left office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned because of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 有文集，頗為世所傳。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings that circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected writings that circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 薛寘，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Zhi was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhi came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖遵顏，魏河東郡守、安邑侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zunyan was Wei Administrator of Hedong commandery and Marquis of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zunyan had served Wei as administrator of Hedong commandery and marquis of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 父乂，清河、廣平二郡守。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Administrator of Qinghe and Guangping commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was administrator of Qinghe and Guangping commanderies.

sentences.zh: 寘幼覽篇籍，好屬文，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: Zhi from youth read books and records, loved literary composition, and began his career as Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhi read widely and loved to write; he began his career as attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 從魏孝武西遷，封郃陽縣子。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei westward in the relocation and was enfeoffed Viscount of Heyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the westward move and was enfeoffed viscount of Heyang county.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元年，領著作佐郎，修國史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei he served concurrently as Assistant Gentleman of the Composing Bureau and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei he served concurrently as assistant gentleman of the composing bureau and compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 尋拜中書侍郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and compiled the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed vice director of the central secretariat and compiled the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 燕公於謹征江陵，以寘為司錄，軍中謀略，寘並參之。

translations.literal: When Duke of Yan Yu Jin campaigned against Jiangling, Zhi was made Chief Clerk; in military stratagems in the army, Zhi participated in all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Yan Yu Jin campaigned against Jiangling, Zhi was made chief clerk and took part in every military plan of the army.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, his rank was advanced to Count.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was pacified, his rank was advanced to count.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方改物創制，欲行《周禮》，乃令寘與小宗伯盧辯斟酌古今，共詳定之。

translations.literal: The court was just then reforming institutions and creating new systems, wishing to implement the 《Rites of Zhou》; it therefore ordered Zhi and Lesser Grand Master of Ancestor Worship Lu Bian to weigh past and present together and jointly work out the details.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then reforming institutions and wished to put the 《Rites of Zhou》 into practice, so it ordered Zhi and lesser grand master of ancestor worship Lu Bian to weigh past and present and jointly work out the details.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授內史下大夫。

translations.literal: When the six offices were established, he was appointed Lower Grand Master of the Inner Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were established, he was appointed lower grand master of the inner secretary.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，進爵為侯，轉禦正中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was advanced to Marquis and transferred to Middle Grand Master of the Imperial Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Zhi was raised to marquis and made middle grand master of the imperial rectifier.

sentences.zh: 時前中書監盧柔，學業優深，文藻華贍，而寘與之方駕，故世號曰盧、薛焉。

translations.literal: At the time the former Director of the Central Secretariat Lu Rou had deep and outstanding scholarship and splendid literary talent; Zhi matched him as an equal, so the age called them Lu and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the former director of the central secretariat Lu Rou was deeply learned and richly gifted in letters; Zhi stood equal with him, so the age spoke of Lu and Xue together.

sentences.zh: 久之，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，出為淅州刺史。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Commander with Staff Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and sent out as Inspector of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the three excellencies, and posted as inspector of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒於位，吏人哀惜之。

translations.literal: He died in office; officials and people mourned and regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post; officials and commoners mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈虞州刺史，諡曰理。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Inspector of Yuzhou; posthumous title Li.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Yuzhou with the posthumous title Li.

sentences.zh: 所著文筆二十餘卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His literary compositions, more than twenty scrolls, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty scrolls of his writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 又撰《西京記》三卷，引據該洽，世稱其博聞焉。

translations.literal: He also compiled the 《Record of the Western Capital》 in three scrolls; its citations were thorough and comprehensive, and the age praised his broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the 《Record of the Western Capital》 in three scrolls; its citations were thorough, and the age praised his wide learning.

sentences.zh: 寘性至孝，雖年齒已衰，職務繁廣，至於溫清之禮，朝夕無違。

translations.literal: Zhi was extremely filial by nature; though advanced in years and burdened with many duties, in the rites of warmth and coolness he never failed morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was deeply filial by nature; though old and burdened with heavy duties, he never missed morning or evening the rites of asking after his parents' warmth and coolness.

sentences.zh: 當時以此稱之。

translations.literal: People of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子明嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ming succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 大象末，儀同大將軍、清水郡守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he was General Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Administrator of Qingshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he was general equal in honor to the three excellencies and administrator of Qingshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 薛憕，字景猷，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Cheng, styled Jingyou, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Cheng, courtesy name Jingyou, came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖弘敞，逢赫連之亂，率宗人避地襄陽。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Hongchang, encountering the turmoil of Helian, led the clan in flight to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Hongchang, during the turmoil of Helian, led the clan in flight to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 憕早喪父，家貧。

translations.literal: Cheng lost his father early; the family was poor.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng lost his father early, and the family was poor.

sentences.zh: 躬耕以養祖母，有暇則覽文籍。

translations.literal: He personally plowed the fields to support his grandmother; when he had spare time he read books and records.
translations.idiomatic: He plowed with his own hands to support his grandmother, and when he had leisure he read books.

sentences.zh: 疏宕不拘，時人未之奇也。

translations.literal: Loose and unrestrained, not bound by convention—men of the time did not yet regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Unconventional and unrestrained, he struck contemporaries as nothing out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 江表取人，多以世族。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi, in selecting men, they mostly relied on hereditary aristocratic families.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi, appointments went chiefly to great clans.

sentences.zh: 憕世無貴仕，解褐不過侍郎。

translations.literal: Cheng's family for generations had no eminent office; when he doffed his hemp-cloth garb his rank did not surpass Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's family had produced no high office for generations, and when he first entered service he rose no higher than vice director.

sentences.zh: 既羈旅，不被擢用。

translations.literal: Being a sojourner, he was not promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: As an outsider living abroad, he went unnoticed and unappointed.

sentences.zh: 常歎曰：「豈能五十年戴幘，死一校尉，低頭傾首，俯仰而向人也！

translations.literal: He often sighed, saying: "How can I spend fifty years wearing an official headcloth and die a mere commandant, bowing my head and bending my neck, rising and falling to defer to others!
translations.idiomatic: He often sighed and said, "Am I to spend fifty years in an official cap and die a mere commandant, bowing and scraping before others in every encounter?

sentences.zh: 」常鬱鬱不得志，每在人間，輒陵架勝達，負才使氣，未嘗趨世祿之門。

translations.literal: " He was constantly depressed and unfulfilled; whenever among people he would tower over and overawe the eminent, relying on his talent and venting his spirit, and never once sought the gates of worldly salary.
translations.idiomatic: " He lived in constant frustration. Among company he would tower over the eminent, trusting in his talent and pride of spirit, and never once sought the doors of men who dispensed worldly salary.

sentences.zh: 左中郎將京兆韋潛度謂曰：「君門地非下，身材不劣，何不{敝衣}裾數參吏部？

translations.literal: Left Middle General Wei Qiandu of Jingzhao said to him: "Your family standing is not low, and your person is not inferior—why not visit the Ministry of Personnel several times in humble dress?
translations.idiomatic: Left middle general Wei Qiandu of Jingzhao said to him, "Your family standing is not low and your person is not inferior—why not visit the Ministry of Personnel several times in humble dress?

sentences.zh: 」憕曰：「'世胄躡高位，英俊沈下寮 '，古人以為歎息，竊所未能也。

translations.literal: " Cheng said: " 'Hereditary scions tread the high posts while outstanding men sink to low offices'—the ancients sighed over this; I personally have not been able to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng replied, " 'Hereditary scions tread the high posts while outstanding men sink to low offices'—the ancients sighed over this, and I myself cannot accept it.

sentences.zh: 」潛度告人曰：「此年少實慷慨，但不遭時耳。」

translations.literal: " Qiandu told others: "This young man is truly spirited and generous—only he has not met the right times."
translations.idiomatic: " Qiandu told others, "This young man is truly high-minded and generous—he simply has not met the right time."

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，杖策還洛陽。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he leaned on his staff and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang he took up his staff and walked home to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 先是憕從祖真度與族祖安都擁徐、兗歸魏，其子懷俊見憕，甚相親善。

translations.literal: Before this, Cheng's paternal cousin Zhendu and clan elder Andu had brought Xu and Yan over to Wei; Zhendu's son Huaijun met Cheng and was very close and friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Cheng's paternal cousin Zhendu and clan elder Andu had brought Xu and Yan over to Wei; Zhendu's son Huaijun met Cheng and became very close to him.

sentences.zh: 屬爾硃榮廢立，怔遂還河東，止懷俊家。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong deposed and enthroned emperors, Cheng then returned to Hedong and stayed at Huaijun's house.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong began deposing and installing emperors, Cheng retreated to Hedong and lodged with Huaijun.

sentences.zh: 不交人物，終日讀書，手自抄略，將二百卷。

translations.literal: He did not associate with others, read all day, and copied extracts with his own hand—nearly two hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He did not associate with others, read all day, and copied extracts in his own hand—nearly two hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 唯郡守元襲時相要屈，與之抗禮。

translations.literal: Only the commandery administrator Yuan Xi from time to time invited and detained him, and Cheng treated him as an equal in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prefect Yuan Xi would sometimes summon him and keep him awhile; Cheng received him as an equal.

sentences.zh: 懷俊每謂曰：「汝還鄉里，不營產業，不肯取妻，豈復欲南乎？

translations.literal: Huaijun often said to him: "You have returned to your homeland, yet build no estate, refuse to take a wife—do you still mean to go south?
translations.idiomatic: Huaijun often said, "You have returned to your homeland, build no property, and refuse to take a wife—do you still mean to go south?

sentences.zh: 」憕亦不介意。

translations.literal: " Cheng also gave it no heed.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng gave it no heed either.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，拜給事中，加伏波將軍。

translations.literal: In the Putai era he was appointed Giving Affairs Attendant and additionally made General Who Pacifies the Waves.
translations.idiomatic: During Putai he was appointed attendant within the gates, with added rank general who pacifies the waves.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武起兵，憕乃東游陳、梁間，謂族人孝通曰：「高歡阻兵陵上，喪亂方始。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised troops, Cheng then traveled east among Chen and Liang and said to his clansman Xiaotong: "Gao Huan blocks the armies and lords it over his sovereign; disorder has only begun.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised troops, Cheng traveled east among Chen and Liang and said to his clansman Xiaotong, "Gao Huan blocks the armies and lords it over his sovereign; disorder has only begun.

sentences.zh: 關中形勝之地，必有霸王據之。

translations.literal: Guanzhong is terrain of strategic advantage; there will surely be a hegemon-king who occupies it.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong is a land of strategic strength; a hegemon is sure to hold it.

sentences.zh: 」乃與孝通俱游長安。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he and Xiaotong together traveled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " So he and his clansman Xiaotong went together to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅聞之，召為行台郎，除鎮遠將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue heard of it, summoned him as Gentleman of the Mobile Staff, and appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distance and Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue heard of it, he summoned Cheng as mobile headquarters gentleman and made him general who pacifies the distance and commandant of foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 及悅害賀拔岳，軍人咸相慶慰。

translations.literal: When Yue killed Heba Yue, the soldiers all congratulated and comforted one another.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue murdered Heba Yue, the troops all congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 憕獨謂所親曰：「悅才略本寡，輒害良將，敗亡之事，其則不遠。

translations.literal: Cheng alone told his intimates: "Yue's talent and strategy were meager to begin with; he rashly killed a fine general—his ruin is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng alone told those close to him, "Yue never had much talent or strategy; by rashly killing a fine general he has brought ruin near.

sentences.zh: 吾屬今即為人所虜，何慶之有乎？

translations.literal: We are about to become others' captives—what is there to celebrate?
translations.idiomatic: We are about to become someone else's prisoners—what is there to celebrate?

sentences.zh: 」長高以憕言為然，並有憂色。

translations.literal: " The people of Chang'an considered Cheng's words correct and all wore worried expressions.
translations.idiomatic: " The people of Chang'an thought Cheng was right and all looked worried.

sentences.zh: 尋而周文平悅，引憕為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Before long Duke Wen of Zhou pacified Yue and brought Cheng in as Recording Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Duke Wen of Zhou crushed Yue and made Cheng recording secretary on his staff.

sentences.zh: 武帝西遷，授征虜將軍、中散大夫，封夏陽縣男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, he was granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Grand Master of Leisurely Dissemination, and enfeoffed Baron of Xiayang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Cheng was made general who punishes the barbarians and grand master of leisurely dissemination, enfeoffed baron of Xiayang county.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，拜中書侍郎，加安東將軍，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he was appointed Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, additionally made General Who Pacifies the East, and advanced to Count.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Cheng was appointed vice director of the central secretariat, given the added rank of general who pacifies the east, and raised to count.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，宣光、清徽殿初成，憕為之頌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, when the Xuan'guang and Qinghui Halls were first completed, Cheng composed encomia for them.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 4, when the Xuanguang and Qinghui halls were first finished, Cheng wrote encomia for them.

sentences.zh: 文帝又造二欹器：一為二仙人共持一缽，同處一盤，缽蓋有山，山有香氣，一仙人又持金瓶以臨器上，傾水灌山，則出於瓶而注乎器，煙氣通發山中，謂之仙人欹器。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen also had two tilting vessels made: one was two immortals jointly holding a bowl, both on one dish; the bowl cover had a mountain with fragrance; one immortal also held a golden flask above the vessel; when water was poured on the mountain it flowed from the flask into the vessel, and smoke issued through the mountain—it was called the Immortals' Tilting Vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen also had two tilting vessels made. One showed two immortals holding a shared bowl on one dish; the bowl's lid bore a fragrant mountain, and one immortal held a golden flask above the vessel; when water was poured on the mountain it ran from the flask into the vessel and smoke rose through the mountain—this was called the Immortals' Tilting Vessel.

sentences.zh: 一為二荷同處一盤，相去盈尺，中有蓮，下垂器上，以水注荷，則出於蓮而盈乎器，為鳧雁蟾以飾之，謂之水芝欹器。

translations.literal: One was two lotuses on one dish, a full chi apart; a lotus hung down over the vessel; when water was poured on the lotus it flowed from the lotus and filled the vessel; ducks, geese, and toads were used as ornament—it was called the Water Lotuses Tilting Vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The other showed two lotuses on one dish a full chi apart, with a lotus hanging down over the vessel; when water was poured on the lotus it flowed out and filled the vessel, ornamented with ducks, geese, and toads—this was called the Water Lotuses Tilting Vessel.

sentences.zh: 二盤各處一床，缽圓而床方，中有人，三才之象也。

translations.literal: The two dishes each rested on a stand; the bowl was round and the stand square, with a human figure between them—the image of the Three Powers.
translations.idiomatic: Each dish stood on its own stand; the bowl was round and the stand square, with a human figure between them to represent heaven, earth, and man.

sentences.zh: 皆置清徽殿前。

translations.literal: Both were placed before the Qinghui Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Both were set before the Qinghui Hall.

sentences.zh: 形似觥而方，滿而平，溢則傾。

translations.literal: Their form resembled a horn cup but was square; when full they stood level, when overflowing they tipped.
translations.idiomatic: The vessels were square like a gong: full they stood level, overflowing they tipped.

sentences.zh: 憕各為頌。

translations.literal: Cheng composed an encomium for each.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wrote an encomium for each.

sentences.zh: 大統初，儀制多闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong many rites and regulations were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong many rites and regulations were still missing.

sentences.zh: 周文令憕與盧辯、檀翥等參定之。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou ordered Cheng together with Lu Bian, Tan Zhu, and others to consult on and fix them.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Zhou ordered Cheng, together with Lu Bian, Tan Zhu, and others, to draft and codify them.

sentences.zh: 以流離世故，不聽音樂，雖幽室獨處，常有戚容。

translations.literal: Because he had been displaced by worldly upheaval, he would not listen to music; even alone in a quiet room he constantly wore a sorrowful expression.
translations.idiomatic: Having been uprooted by the turmoil of the age, he would not listen to music; even alone in a quiet room he often looked sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 後坐事死。

translations.literal: Later he was executed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 子舒嗣，官至禮部下大夫、儀同大將軍、聘陳使副。

translations.literal: His son Shu succeeded; he reached the office of Lower Grand Master of the Ministry of Rites, General Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and deputy envoy on the mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu succeeded him and rose to lower grand master in the Ministry of Rites, general equal in honor to the three excellencies, and deputy envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 論曰：薛辯有魏之初，功業早樹，門膺人爵，無替榮名。

translations.literal: Commentary says: At the beginning of Wei, Xue Bian early established merit and achievement; his house received noble ranks from the throne, without lapse in glorious reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: At the beginning of Wei, Xue Bian early established merit and achievement; his house received noble ranks from the throne, and its glorious name never faded.

sentences.zh: 端以謙直見知；

translations.literal: Duan was known for modesty and straightforwardness;
translations.idiomatic: Duan was known for modesty and forthrightness;

sentences.zh: 胄以公平自命。

translations.literal: Zhou prided himself on fairness and impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou prided himself on fairness and impartiality.

sentences.zh: 浚之孝悌，素緒之所得也。

translations.literal: Jun's filial piety and brotherly devotion were what a plain lineage could achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's filial piety and brotherly devotion were what a plain lineage could achieve.

sentences.zh: 道衡雅道弈葉，世擅文宗，令望攸歸，豈徒然矣。

translations.literal: Daoheng's elegant Way passed down leaf by leaf like a Go game; generation after generation the family monopolized literary eminence, and all lofty reputation converged upon him—was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng's elegant craft passed down generation after generation like leaves on a Go board; the family monopolized literary eminence, and all lofty reputation converged upon him—was it for nothing?

sentences.zh: 而運逢季叔，卒蹈誅戮，痛乎！

translations.literal: Yet his fate met the season's younger decline; in the end he suffered execution—how painful!
translations.idiomatic: Yet fate met a season of decline; in the end he suffered execution—how painful!

sentences.zh: 仲良任惟繁劇，弘益流譽；

translations.literal: Zhongliang took on only heavy and urgent duties, spreading broad benefit and flowing reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang took on only the heaviest duties and won wide renown for the good he accomplished;

sentences.zh: 而陷齊諂護，以要權寵，易名為繆，斯豈虛哉！

translations.literal: yet he fell into informing on Qi and fawning on Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu to seek power and favor—his posthumous name was changed to Miu; was this undeserved!
translations.idiomatic: yet he informed on Qi Gui and flattered Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu to win power and favor—his posthumous name was changed to Miu; was that not fitting!

sentences.zh: 寘、憕並學稱該博，文擅雕龍，或揮翰鳳池，或著書麟閣，咸居祿位，各逞琳琅。

translations.literal: Zhi and Cheng together were acclaimed in scholarship as comprehensive and broad, excelled in literary craft like carving dragons; some wielded the brush at the Phoenix Pool, some authored books at the Unicorn Pavilion—all held salary office, each displaying brilliant talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Cheng were both praised as broadly learned and masters of literary craft; some wrote at the Phoenix Pool, others compiled works at the Unicorn Pavilion—all held office and each shone with talent.

sentences.zh: 擬彼徐、陳，慚後生之可畏；

translations.literal: Compared with those Xu and Chen, one would feel shame at how formidable the younger generation is;
translations.idiomatic: Set beside the famous Xu and Chen, one would feel humbled by how formidable this younger generation was;

sentences.zh: 論其任遇，實當時之良選也。

translations.literal: Speaking of their appointments and treatment, they were truly the fine choices of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by their appointments and honors, they were truly the best men of their time.
